commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Every release now ships with its own SBOM, committed and uploaded
details: ICTU recommendation 10 asks for SBOMs of released versions, kept analysable: when an advisory lands against something that shipped months ago, the question is what that version contained, and only a document written at the time answers it. scripts/write-sbom.mjs (npm run sbom) writes docs/sbom/<name>-<version>.cdx.json — CycloneDX, production dependencies only, read from the lockfile without installing. It is now a step in bump-release, after the version bump, since the filename carries the version.

sbom.yml runs on a push to main, on demand, and on pull requests that touch the tooling. A promotion to main is the release here, so it uploads the document as an artifact and asserts the released version has one. Two copies because neither suffices alone: artifacts expire after ninety days on a public repository, so the committed copy is the durable one; the artifact is what a scanner can fetch without a checkout.

Three modes: writing; --check, strict, for where the release is cut; and --verify-release for the promotion, where a missing document fails but drift only warns, because a promotion carries every commit merged since the release. Both comparisons parse the JSON and ignore serialNumber and timestamp, so Prettier reformatting the file changes nothing.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The lockfile-sync check no longer fails on a clean checkout
details: The new step failed on every pull request, and not for the reason it exists: npm ci --dry-run still runs lifecycle scripts, and the root postinstall copies package-lock.json into node_modules, which a dry run never creates. On a clean checkout that is ENOENT, reported under a step named "Lockfile matches package.json" — precisely the confusion the step was added to remove. It passed locally only because that machine already had node_modules.
--ignore-scripts skips the postinstall. Whether the lockfile satisfies package.json is decided before any script runs, so the check keeps its meaning.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: A lockfile that disagrees with package.json now fails under its own name
details: npm ci already refused such a lockfile, but only as an EUSAGE error inside "Install dependencies for the formatter", three steps into a job about pinning. It happened on 25 September 2026 in ronl-business-api: three dependency pull requests merged back to back, each green against its own base, produced a lockfile matching no package.json.

An npm ci --dry-run step now runs before that install, costs seconds, and fails with the cause in its own name. What it cannot catch is recorded next to it: it proves consistency with the pull request's own base, not with a base that has moved since. Merge dependency pull requests one at a time, rebasing each onto the merged acc first.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The ubuntu 26.04 runner major is deferred, with its reason recorded
details: ICTU recommendation 7 asks for a major to be assessed and the decision recorded. ubuntu 26.04 was assessed on 24 September 2026 and held by a Renovate rule carrying its reason and the condition that ends it: the runner pins exist to stop the image drifting, and ubuntu-latest still resolves to 24.04. Revisit when it moves.

The other queued majors — react-router-dom 7, vitest 5, jsdom 30, vite 8, typescript 7, eslint 10, React and the grouped workspace majors — are deliberately not disabled. They stay behind Dependency Dashboard approval, where a person sees them.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Renovate never offers a new major's X.0.0 release
details: ICTU recommendation 7 also asks to wait for the first or second patch of a major. Majors already wait for Dependency Dashboard approval; nothing said which version may be offered once approved. An allowedVersions rule for the npm manager now excludes X.0.0, so the earliest a major can arrive is X.0.1.

Scoped to npm because the same pattern against Docker tags or runner images would mean something else. Validated with renovate-config-validator --strict and against fourteen versions; every major queued today is unaffected. The cost is recorded in the rule: a package that never patches its X.0.0 needs a per-package exception.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The daily audit's job is named dependency-audit, so it no longer collides with the required audit check
details: audit is zizmor.yml's job and a required status check. Required checks match by name, so a second job of that name made the context ambiguous — one passing and one failing check under one name, which no ruleset can satisfy. Its first run blocked sgort/ronl-business-api#206 outright. SECURITY-PIPELINE.md now names the check alongside the rest of the audit's specification.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The daily audit runs its script from a path the branch checkouts cannot remove
details: The audit loop checks out origin/acc and origin/main in turn, replacing the working tree — including scripts/audit-tree.mjs itself. The first run lost the script at the first checkout, and node's missing-module exit was read as "a high or critical advisory was found".

The script is now copied to $RUNNER_TEMP before the loop. Each iteration resets its own status and anything above 2 is clamped to 2, so "the audit could not run" can never be mistaken for a finding or for a clean tree.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Dependencies are audited daily, on both acc and main
details: Every other gate runs on a commit, so a new advisory against unchanged code was seen by nothing, and Dependabot watches acc rather than the main that production deploys from. dependency-audit.yml runs at 05:17 UTC and on demand, reading each branch's lockfile with npm audit --package-lock-only. It fails on a high or critical advisory in production dependencies, reports the rest, and opens, updates and closes one tracking issue so a scheduled failure reaches someone. ICTU recommendation 10.

scripts/audit-tree.mjs groups findings by advisory rather than by package: on 24 September this repository's 28 moderate entries were three advisories, 24 of them the same @tiptap/core. An audit that cannot run exits 2 and is treated as a finding, never as a clean tree.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The quality service's tag matcher only accepts its three known tags
details: Semgrep's detect-non-literal-regexp flagged both RegExps in matchTag, which interpolate its tag parameter. The parameter was string, so only the call sites kept data out of the pattern. It is now a MeasuredTag union of exactly 'decision', 'uitvoeringsregel' and 'inputData', so the compiler enforces what a comment used to assert.

Both lines carry a scoped nosemgrep naming the rule, why it is safe, and what would end that: widening the type back to string. Neither pattern has a nested quantifier, so there was no backtracking risk either way.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The promotion drift guard's failure message uses a constant format string
details: Semgrep unsafe-formatstring, low. With a second argument, console.error passes the first to util.format, so the interpolated workflow and target names became part of a format string — a %s in either would consume the path list. Not exploitable, since both come from a hardcoded array, but that assumption is what stops being true when someone derives the list from a directory read.
The values now go in as arguments behind a constant format string, with %j for the path list. A forced failure still reports correctly; npm run test:scripts passes.

commits.author: renovate[bot]
commits.subject: concurrently updated to v10
details: Root dev dependency used to run the frontend and backend dev servers together. A tooling-only change; nothing it touches is deployed.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: A promotion runs the three production deploys in order instead of racing them
details: Each production workflow used to trigger itself on a push to main with its own paths: filter, and the three started at once. On the v2026.09.6 promotion the ROPA site finished deploying to production before the backend had started building — production served new pages against the previous API for several minutes, under three green checks. Nothing broke, and nothing would have caught it either.

promote-to-production.yml is now the only thing a push to main starts. It calls the three deploys as reusable workflows: a changes job decides what is needed, the backend goes first, then the two sites in parallel. A failed backend stops both sites; a skipped one does not, so each site checks the backend's result against a positive list rather than just "not failed".

The path filters had to leave the triggers — a filter per workflow cannot express "the sites wait for the backend". They live in scripts/promotion-targets.mjs, with a test beside it that the promotion's own changes job runs before using the script. Four of its checks are a drift guard: the two site workflows still carry those paths on the pull_request trigger that builds the production preview, and the test fails if the two stop agreeing. It fails safe towards deploying everything — a promotion whose commit range cannot be read is not a promotion that changed nothing.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The production-site preview on a promotion pull request is a decision, not an oversight
details: The two production site workflows carry a pull_request trigger on main, so opening a promotion pull request deploys a preview of the production site built from acc. That was recorded as an open question; it is now recorded as kept, deliberately. The point is to look at the real thing before promoting rather than infer it from an acceptance build.

The costs are written down with the decision: a public URL on a production resource serving unreleased code, an environment slot on the production app, and a teardown that depends on the close job running — which GitHub will not run while a pull request has a merge conflict. The backend is excluded on purpose, and that asymmetry is the decision rather than an oversight: a preview site is a page to look at, a preview backend on production would be a second live API against production data.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Every deploy check runs, instead of the first failure hiding the rest
details: "Verify v1 endpoints" ran five hard assertions, each exiting on failure, so the first to fail stopped the rest from running. On the v2026.09.6 promotion the OpenAPI/health version comparison failed inside the deploy's stale window and exited — so the native-binding assertion below it never executed, and had the binding been broken nothing would have said so. A soft consistency check suppressed a hard correctness one.

Each exit now records a failure and the step fails at the end if any of them did, so every assertion runs and the log shows all the failures rather than the first. Collecting rather than reordering, deliberately: reordering only changes which check gets to mask the rest.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The two production site deploy jobs have names that can be told apart
details: Both production site workflows named their deploy job "Build and Deploy Job". Required checks are matched by job name, so while both answered to one name neither could be required, referenced, or distinguished in a check list — the v2026.09.6 promotion pull request showed two identical rows. They are now "Build and Deploy Production Frontend" and "Build and Deploy Production ROPA Site".

The same defect was fixed on the ACC side earlier; the production pair was never renamed with it. This changes no ruleset — main requires audit and scan only — so it is a precondition rather than a fix in itself: it is what makes requiring, sequencing or referencing these jobs possible at all.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: build-info.json is read at module load, closing a false pass in the deploy gate
details: getBuildInfo() read the file lazily, on first use, and its comment said the file "cannot change without a redeploy, which restarts the process". It can. A zip deploy overwrites build-info.json while the previous process is still serving, and the restart comes afterwards — so the old process read the new file the first time anything asked, and the first thing to ask is the deploy's own build.sha check. That is a false pass in the gate whose entire purpose is to prove the new build is serving.

Seen on the v2026.09.6 promotion: two seconds apart, one process reported /v1/openapi.json at 2026.09.6 and /v1/health at 2026.09.5. version comes from an import bound at module load and still read the previous release; build.sha was read from disk afterwards and got the new one. The App Service plan is B1 with capacity 1, so two instances cannot explain it — an earlier guess that they might was wrong.
The read now happens at module load, so both answers are bound at the same moment and a stale process reports itself as stale.

commits.author: renovate[bot]
commits.subject: lint-staged 16 to 17
details: A major bump to the tool the pre-commit hook runs. Verified beyond the suite by staging a deliberately mis-formatted file and running the hook end to end: prettier and eslint --fix both ran, the file was reformatted and restaged, and the hook exited 0.

commits.author: renovate[bot]
commits.subject: Frontend dependencies: @types/react 19.3, @types/node and autoprefixer
details: Type and tooling updates only — nothing that ships at runtime. @types/react and @types/react-dom move 19.2 to 19.3, which is the one here that could have surfaced type errors; typecheck, the full suite and the production build are clean.

commits.author: renovate[bot]
commits.subject: Backend dependencies: @types/n3 and typescript-eslint 8.70
details: A types patch and a typescript-eslint minor. Lint is clean on the new version, which is the check that matters for an eslint bump — a minor there can introduce rules that fail an existing tree.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Shared DSO constants move out of shared.tsx
details: shared.tsx exported constants, a type and a helper next to the Section component, which react-refresh/only-export-components flags six times: Fast Refresh cannot hot-swap a module that exports non-components. They move unchanged to tokens.ts; shared.tsx keeps Section.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Thuisbatterij processes in swimlanes, with Dutch names and a missing-info form
details: Both processes get a pool and Aanvrager/Behandelaar/Systeem lanes, matching the shape the RIPx.y processes already have. Element ids are unchanged; names become Dutch.

"Aanvullende gegevens opvragen" pointed at an embedded HTML form that never existed, so nothing could set supplementReceived; it now uses a deployable form-js form. Seeds are bumped so the Modeler replaces cached copies.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The register records zizmor-action v0.6.4 and the validator's Node 24.21.0
details: The audit job failed on the action-bump branch because the workflow pinned v0.6.4 while SECURITY-PIPELINE.md still recorded v0.6.3. That is the documented drift rather than a fault in the bump: Renovate rewrites a workflow pin and its version comment together and never touches the register, so every action-bump pull request fails the register half until it is updated by hand — on the bump's own branch, so the check is green on the pull request rather than only on acc afterwards.
The action-and-image pairing the file warns about held: v0.6.4 ran the pinned 1.29.0 image without complaint, so this does not drag in the image bump that has to move with the action.

commits.author: renovate[bot]
commits.subject: zizmor-action 0.6.4 and the validator's Node to 24.21.0
details: The workflow pin itself, paired with the register rows above. Nothing in the repository's own supply-chain posture changes; this keeps the auditor and the Node it runs on current.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The native binding is verified on the deployed app, not just on the runner
details: "Prepare deployment package" already asserted that require('libxmljs2') loads, but it runs on the runner — so it proves the binary matches the Node that built it. Nothing proved it loads on the host. Those are the same question only while the two agree, and on 23 September they stopped agreeing: the Node 24 move left a Node-22 binary answering on a Node-24 host, and DMN validation returned NODE_MODULE_VERSION 127 against a required 137 while health, build.sha, the shape layers and /v1/dmns all reported fine.

Both backend workflows now POST a minimal DMN to /v1/dmns/validate on the deployed app and fail on the native-load signature. Read-only — that endpoint validates content and deploys nothing — and it fails only on a message naming NODE_MODULE_VERSION or "was compiled against", never on a DMN that is merely invalid, so it cannot start failing because the XSD tightens or the fixture drifts.

commits.author: renovate[bot]
commits.subject: Node moves to 24.21.0
details: One line in .nvmrc, 22.23.2 to 24.21.0, which every deploy workflow reads. Held open since 19 September because merging it alone would have built the backend on Node 24 and run it on a NODE|22-lts App Service; the decision recorded against #119 is that Azure offers major-level runtimes only, so the control is the ordering — switch the App Service first, then merge.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The child-activity fan-out is capped, and stops writing after teardown
details: Opening an activity fired one request per child simultaneously — 24 at once for a 23-child parent. The backend cache removed the repeat cost; this removes the burst. Five workers pull from a shared cursor, so the same work arrives in waves, and allSettled semantics are kept: a failing child never blocks the rest, and one that resolves without an omschrijving still falls back to its URN. Names now appear as each child resolves rather than when the slowest does.

The component had no cancellation guard at all — not a flag, not an AbortController — so an in-flight fan-out could write names for an activity the user had already left. That was latent while everything raced to finish at once; a pool drains over time, which would have made it real.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Six weak assertions are made to bite
details: Each named a behaviour it could not fail on. The TTL boundary at exactly ttlMs was pinned by nothing, so the > versus >= choice was free; an entry aged exactly the TTL is now asserted live, because expiring it there would quietly shave time off every advertised TTL. clear() with no key asserted one key was gone rather than the cache being empty. The cache-hit test compared an object with itself, so it could not fail for the reason its name gave.

The wId assertion checked a prefix, so a truncation past that point would have passed. The openTags guard stays and is now commented as deliberately unreachable, with tests pinning the outward guarantee instead — decisionTable is never counted as a decision, prefixed or not — so the protection survives whichever mechanism enforces it.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The regelingen search pages, honours the date, and names what failed
details: The search read only page one. mnre1034 already returns a full page of 100, so an authority's instrument could fall off it and be reported as "no regeling of type …" — a wrong answer rather than an error. It now pages by page.totalPages, sequentially, capped at 10, and a cap-truncated search is recorded distinctly from a genuine miss.

getToepasbareRegels ignored the validity date, so a dossier for a past date paired a historical legal source with current executable rules, then took toepasbareRegels[0] with no ordering guarantee. The date now threads through in the same dd-MM-yyyy the other RTR-side calls use, and the pick is by most recent begindatum rather than by position.

Three of the four fan-out legs recorded failures without saying which item failed; documentComponent, dmn and toepasbareRegels now carry the wId, the rule identifier and the functioneleStructuurRef respectively. Also: stats() no longer counts expired entries.

commits.author: renovate[bot]
commits.subject: Frontend dependencies updated
details: A routine Renovate refresh of the frontend's dependency ranges, held for the 14-day cooldown like everything else.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The CI posture page records 23 September
details: The first real promotion sequenced by a workflow rather than by hand, with its timings: the backend ran 16:53:18 to 17:00:09 and all three site jobs started four seconds after it completed, where previously they would have finished about five minutes before the backend they depend on. Also the App Service runtime decision — Azure offers major-level Node runtimes only, so the control is the ordering — and the container-image split by whether a repository actually applies the file.

Plus the exception that this repository is: `switch first, then merge` is complete only for a pure-JavaScript backend, and libxmljs2 builds against NAN rather than N-API, so its binary is bound to NODE_MODULE_VERSION.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: A taxonomy node's empty dossier points at its children
details: An activity that groups others carries no rules of its own, so its dossier is correctly empty — but that told the reader nothing about where the rules actually are. The Dossier now carries childActivityUrns, taken from the RTR response step 1 already fetches, so it costs no extra upstream calls.

Where both rule sets are absent and children exist, the Quality Profile tab says so and lists them as links that load the child's own profile. An activity with children and rules of its own is not a taxonomy node and does not get the notice. For Rijksmonumentenactiviteit that means the empty dossier now points at RijksmonArchMonument and RijkmonMonument, which carry a Conclusie and Indieningsvereisten each.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The per-bestuurslaag lookup and the Quality Profile tab are documented
details: The method doc said --authority was required for a national activity and that its absence returned a 400. Both became false with the fix. It also described the regeling lookup as omgevingsplan-only, which was the defect underneath — each bestuurslaag has its own core instrument, and looking for an omgevingsplan at provincie, waterschap or rijk level finds nothing.

Adds the per-level table, the multi-candidate probe and its cap, taxonomy nodes as a named edge case, and wording that distinguishes a regeling checked and found not to annotate an activity from one that could not be fetched at all. The API doc gains a section for the Quality Profile tab.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The production level-derivation path is covered, and provenance stops overclaiming
details: Every test built bestuursorgaan without a bestuurslaag field, so all of them exercised the code-prefix fallback while production takes the other branch — the RTR does supply bestuurslaag. A case where the two disagree now pins which wins, and bestuurslaag is validated against the known levels instead of being trusted through a bare type assertion.

When a candidate regeling could not be fetched, the summary still said none of them annotate the activity — asserting a negative about a document that was never read. Checked-and-not-matching is now reported separately from could-not-be-fetched, and each fetch failure names its candidate. A reader can tell "we looked and it is not there" from "we could not look", which is what makes a partial dossier honest rather than broken.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: A legal source resolves per bestuurslaag, and national activities are no longer rejected
details: The dossier refused any mnre URN without an authority parameter. That guard was ours, not a DSO requirement, and it rejected activities that needed nothing: RijksmonArchMonument carries its own Conclusie and Indieningsvereisten and scores 23/23 semantic, yet returned 400. The advice it gave was also wrong — no municipality can supply a national activity's legal source.

The lookup also hardcoded regelingtype_003, the gemeente instrument, so for any provincie, waterschap or rijk activity it searched for a document type that authority never publishes. Each bestuurslaag has its own: Omgevingsplan, Omgevingsverordening, Waterschapsverordening, AMvB. The level comes from bestuursorgaan.bestuurslaag, falling back to the authority code prefix, and an explicit authority still overrides it. Where several regelingen of the right type exist — the Rijk publishes two AMvBs — they are tried in order, capped at three because each annotation graph can be megabytes.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The Level select stays in step with the preserved authority
details: The Authority select's options come from authoritiesByLevel(level) while its value is authorityOin, which now survives a tab switch. level did not: it was ActiviteitenTab-local and reset on every remount. So choosing provincie and an authority within it, then returning to Activities, left the select showing a value that was not among its own options — blank, while the list below still showed that authority's activities. Lifting level alongside the others needs no new restore logic; it simply stops being reset.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: A comparison fetches with the compared authority, and the authority survives a tab switch
details: The Compare fetch passed the primary activity's bevoegd-gezag code for the compared URN. The backend treats authority as an override, so comparing Lelystad with Steenwijkerland searched Lelystad's regelingen for a Steenwijkerland activity: the compared card read "Steenwijkerland — Omgevingsplan gemeente Lelystad" with 0/10 rules traced, for an activity that has two. Only the legal-source half was affected; the matrix columns were already correct.
Returning to the Activities tab no longer clears the selected authority. Adds a Clear compare control beside Dossier .md, shown only while a comparison is active.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: A quality-profile teaser in the detail panel, and a Dossier .md download
details: The activity detail panel gains a compact quality-profile section, summing both rule sets into one decision-naming and one input-naming row. That is the only place the two are combined: it is a teaser pointing at the tab, not a score, and the tab itself still keeps them separate.

It renders from cache only. The dossier call fans out across three upstream APIs including Ozon, so selecting an activity must never trigger it — there is a test asserting exactly that, because the failure mode is a detail panel that feels broken. renderDossier moves to scripts/dossier-render.mjs, imported by both the CLI and the browser, with a test asserting the two references are the same function object rather than merely producing equal output, so the two cannot drift apart.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The Quality Profile tab
details: Renders the selected activity's quality profile with the evidence behind every number: per-item naming classes, each input's question, and the legal-source articles. Scorecard is the default layout; Compare uses the matrix, which keeps the two authorities in separate columns.

Conclusie and Indieningsvereisten are always shown separately and never blended into one score, and a rule set that is absent says so rather than reporting zeros — zeros would read as measured-and-empty. The authority filter sends the bevoegd-gezag code, not the OIN: the backend matches it against bevoegdGezag, so an OIN would have silently failed the national-activity path that needs it.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The activity selection is shared across DSO Explorer tabs
details: selectedUrn, the active validity date and authorityOin move from ActiviteitenTab up into DsoExplorer, so a tab other than Activities can read the current selection. Switching tabs no longer clears it; changing Level or Authority, clicking Load, and closing the detail panel all still do.
ActivityDetailPanel gains an onLoaded callback so the selected activity's name reaches the shell whichever way it was selected — row click, pasted URN, or parent/child navigation.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: A frontend client for the activity dossier endpoint
details: Mirrors the backend Dossier and QualityProfile types and adds getActiviteitDossier, with an in-memory cache keyed env|datum|urn so switching to the Quality Profile tab is instant. The dossier call fans out across three upstream APIs including Ozon, so it is slow enough that an uncached tab switch would be felt. The cache stores the promise rather than the resolved value, so concurrent calls for the same key dedupe, and evicts on failure so a retry is not permanently blocked by one bad response.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The evidence behind the quality profile's counts is shown
details: The profile reported counts without saying which items scored how, so "3/7 semantic, 4 opaque" could not be audited by the municipality whose data it describes. The per-item naming classes, each input's question and the legal-source articles now travel with the numbers.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The datum format contract, GUID detection, cache eviction and cross-layer scoring
details: The datum parameter was forwarded unchanged to two upstreams using different date formats: the RTR expects dd-MM-yyyy, Ozon expects YYYY-MM-dd. No value satisfied both, and the failure was silent — the annotations leg was caught into provenance.failures while legalSource.available stayed true, rendering a real regeling title above "0 juridische regels". The route keeps dd-MM-yyyy and converts before calling Ozon.

GUID detection required separators, but IMOW URN local names are 32 contiguous hex characters, so GUID-named activities scored as semantic — the exact case the quality profile exists to surface. The tag scanner hardcoded the dmn: prefix, silently reporting an un-prefixed DMN as having nothing opaque. Cross-layer consistency compared two layers where the design defines three. And the TTL cache never evicted entries that were not read again, retaining an 8.7 MB annotation graph per municipality for the process lifetime.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The dossier CLI runs on Windows, and the new modules' branches are covered
details: A path-handling fix in scripts/dso-dossier.mjs, and coverage for the branches the four new modules had left untested — the dossier service, the Ozon client, the quality service and the TTL cache, together about 350 lines of new test.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The activity dossier method and a worked example
details: docs/dso-activity-dossier.md sets out how an activity's chain is assembled and scored, and docs/examples/dossier-houtopstandvellen-gm0995.md is the rendered output for a real activity, so the method can be read against a concrete result rather than in the abstract.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: CDATA is preserved in rendered article text
details: Article text arrives wrapped in CDATA and was being lost in the Markdown render. The renderer now preserves it, and the render tests are tightened around the cases that let it through.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: An activity dossier and its quality profile render to Markdown
details: scripts/dso-dossier.mjs turns a dossier into a readable document — legal source, annotations, decision criteria, submission requirements and the quality profile — so a result can be circulated and reviewed outside the app.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The activity dossier is exposed with its quality profile
details: The composite route that joins the three upstream legs into one Dossier and returns it with its QualityProfile, described in the OpenAPI document alongside the passthrough routes it builds on.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Activity-identity resolvability is derived, not assumed
details: The quality profile treated an activity's identity as resolvable by construction. It is now derived from what the lookup actually returned, so an identity that cannot be resolved scores as such rather than being credited.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: An activity's legibility and recoverability are scored
details: quality.service.ts scores the assembled chain on two separate axes — how legible the rules are, and how far a reader can recover the reasoning from the published material. Kept apart deliberately: blending them into one number would hide which of the two is weak.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The dossier join is made falsifiable with real decoy annotations
details: The join's tests used a fixture clean enough that a wrong join would still have passed. The fixture now carries real decoy annotations from the production graph — nearly 600 lines of them — so a join that matches the wrong thing fails.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: An activity's legal source, annotation and rule sets are assembled
details: dossier.service.ts is the join: it takes an IMOW activity and assembles its legal source, its annotations, and both rule sets into a single Dossier. The join is isolated in one service by design, so the fan-out across three upstream APIs has exactly one place that knows how the pieces fit together.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The Ozon routes are asserted to conform to their OpenAPI operations
details: The three passthrough routes are checked against the operations that describe them, so the document and the implementation cannot drift apart silently.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The three Ozon Presenteren routes the dossier needs are proxied
details: The chain spans a sixth DSO API that this backend did not proxy: Omgevingsdocumenten Presenteren (Ozon). Three passthrough routes are added, described in the OpenAPI document, with the existing DSO keys authenticating against it.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: An Omgevingsdocumenten Presenteren v8 client
details: ozon.service.ts, the client for Ozon v8.5.2, with the quirks the plan front-loaded: the full OGC Content-Crs value, the slash-to-underscore identificatie transform, and environment-specific toepasbare-regel ids.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: dsoFetch defaults to POST when a body is supplied
details: A one-line correction with its test: supplying a body no longer silently issues a GET.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Ozon base URLs, and dsoFetch learns POST bodies and extra headers
details: The shared DSO fetch helper gains what the Ozon calls need — a request body and additional headers — and the Ozon base URLs join the configuration beside the existing DSO ones.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Shared cache stats and clears are verified against the DMN caches
details: The cache routes report and clear across the named registry. This pins that the DMN caches are actually part of that registry, rather than the endpoints reporting on a subset while appearing to cover everything.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Activity detail is cached, removing the fan-out's repeat cost
details: The DSO Explorer's child-activity fan-out asked for the same details repeatedly. Caching the activity-detail lookup removes the repeat cost; the burst itself is capped separately.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: A shared TTL cache utility with a named registry
details: Replaces a second hand-rolled cache with one utility, registered by name so the cache routes can report and clear across every cache rather than a hardcoded list. Front-loaded deliberately: it is independently valuable and lands before any dossier code.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Implementation plan for the activity dossier
details: Ten tasks, TDD throughout, front-loading the independently valuable work: the shared TTL cache and the activity-detail caching land before any dossier code. Global constraints carry the quirks each task inherits — both GUID separators, CDATA question text, the slash-to-underscore identificatie transform, the full OGC Content-Crs value, and environment-specific toepasbare-regel ids.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Design for the activity dossier, quality profile and shared cache
details: The design for assembling an IMOW activity's full chain — legal source, annotations, decision criteria, submission requirements — as a single call, and for scoring how legible that chain is. The chain spans a sixth DSO API this repository does not proxy, Omgevingsdocumenten Presenteren v8.5.2; the existing DSO keys already authenticate against it. Three passthrough routes plus one composite route, with the join isolated in a single service.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The CI posture page records 19–22 September and drops 14 closed rows
details: Four days of work across all three repositories were unrecorded, and section 6 was carrying rows for fourteen issues that are closed. Adds the dated section and removes them, each checked against the GitHub API rather than inferred.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The e2e fixture bundle declares and ships the decisions it depends on
details: The manifest described bpmn, forms, documents and subProcesses, and shipped no .dmn at all — while every process in the bundle calls decisions. A stack rebuilt from the documented bundle therefore deployed cleanly, served its start forms cleanly, and then failed at the first business rule task with "no decision definition deployed with key 'AwbCompletenessCheck'". One key at a time, four rounds of the same discovery, with nothing in the bundle to suggest a DMN was ever involved.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The Thuisbatterij bundle is seeded into the Modeler
details: The Thuisbatterij files sat in public/examples/flevoland/ but stopped there: fetchable by URL and invisible in the app, with no entry in the version registry, no block in the BPMN Modeler's seeding, no form definitions and no document template. It was the only bundle in public/examples with no way into the UI, which left deploying it a file-shuffling exercise rather than the Modeler flow kapvergunning and zorgtoeslag already have.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Thuisbatterij forms are bound to their deployment
details: Thuisbatterij was the one bundle still on camunda:formRefBinding="latest" for all three forms. With latest, Operaton resolves a form by key across deployments, and on a long-lived engine that key is not unique. On ACC that form key sits in 53 deployments — 50 untenanted from June and July, 3 under flevoland — so the start form 500s and the citizen dashboard shows "Formulier kon niet worden geladen" with no field ever rendering. Kapvergunning is immune purely because its forms are already deployment-bound.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Tenant-scoped processes reach the shared, untenanted DMNs
details: Operaton resolves a business rule task's decisionRef inside the process instance's own tenant. A process deployed under tenant-id 'flevoland' therefore cannot see a DMN deployed without one, and the engine refuses to instantiate it at all — surfacing as a 500 from process start and an unexplained "De aanvraag kon niet worden ingediend" on the ACC citizen dashboard. Kapvergunning was broken this way; Thuisbatterij had the same defect one step further in, pinned to a tenant id.

commits.author: renovate[bot]
commits.subject: Lock-file maintenance
details: The weekly refresh of package-lock.json. Every version it introduced was at least 14 days old when the branch was written, measured against the npm registry's own publish dates.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: A change to .nvmrc builds and deploys
details: .nvmrc sets the Node version every deploy workflow builds, tests and ships on, and no path filter included it. A Node bump therefore built nothing, tested nothing and deployed nothing: the new Node reached the next unrelated deploy untested. Once the build checks became required on acc, such a pull request also showed every required build check skipped and was mergeable. Found on #80, which changes .nvmrc alone.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The build checks now required on acc are written down
details: SECURITY-PIPELINE.md records which checks gate acc and main, why the build checks are safe to require now that each workflow filters in a changes job rather than on its trigger, and that renaming one of those jobs means updating the ruleset in the same change. Being documentation only, the pull request was also the test: every changes job reported relevant false and every build check skipped.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: ACC deploy workflows filter in a job, so their build checks can be required
details: A required check must report on every pull request. A workflow its pull_request trigger filters out never starts and reports nothing, so a required build check would leave any pull request that does not touch its paths waiting forever. A job skipped by its own if: reports success instead.

Each ACC deploy workflow drops the path filter from its trigger and gains a changes job, which asks the GitHub API for the pull request's files — renames under both names — and matches them against one pattern mirroring the push filter. The build and close jobs run when relevant, and also when changes did not succeed, so a failed lookup means a full build rather than a free pass. The two jobs both named Build and Deploy Job become Build and Deploy Frontend and Build and Deploy ROPA Site, since required checks are matched by job name.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: A 14-day package-manager cooldown in .npmrc
details: Renovate's minimumReleaseAge covers only the updates Renovate proposes. Lock-file maintenance hands the refresh to npm, where the transitive tree moves, and Renovate documents that its own cooldown cannot apply there. A root .npmrc now sets min-release-age=14.

Measured before writing it: npm 11.10 or newer honours the setting on install and update and refuses an exact pin to a younger version with ETARGET; npm ci ignores it on purpose, so CI cannot fail on it; npm 10.9.8 ignores it without a warning. scripts/check-deps.sh now warns, without failing, when npm is older than 11.10.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The directory npm leaves behind is empty, not full of hidden entries
details: The comment added with the un-hoisted guard said the runner's packages/backend/node_modules holds hidden npm bookkeeping. The run that passed logged its contents, and it was empty: npm 10 leaves the directory behind with nothing in it. The guard was right either way, since it counts only real package entries; the explanation was not.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Only real packages count as un-hoisted backend dependencies
details: The guard failed whenever packages/backend/node_modules existed, so the first run of the new packaging step failed on a correct install: "added 350 packages", then the guard, listing nothing. It now fails only on a non-hidden entry, which is what a real un-hoisted package would be, and always logs what the directory holds.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The backend deploy installs its dependencies from the lockfile
details: Both backend workflows assembled deploy/ with package.json and no lockfile, then ran npm install --production there, re-resolving every caret range at deploy time with no cooldown. The shipped artifact could carry versions no test ran against and no lockfile records.

The step now runs npm ci --omit=dev --workspace=@linked-data-explorer/backend in a staging copy holding the root manifest and lockfile and the backend's manifest, and copies that node_modules into deploy/. Measured: 349 packages, each at the root lockfile's version and integrity hash. Install scripts still run, since libxmljs2 is native; the step checks that its binding loads, and fails if a production dependency lands un-hoisted where the copy would drop it.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The runner image is pinned to ubuntu-24.04
details: All twelve jobs across the eight workflows run on ubuntu-24.04 instead of ubuntu-latest, a label GitHub moves to a new Ubuntu release on its own schedule. A change of OS release now arrives as a diff in this repository. That pins the release, not the image — GitHub rebuilds it about weekly and a hosted runner cannot be pinned by digest — so Node, actions and npm packages stay pinned separately.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The frontend builds on the runner, and Node is read from one .nvmrc
details: Both frontend workflows now run build:acc / build:prod on the runner, from the tree npm ci installed, and upload packages/frontend/dist with skip_app_build: true. Until now Oryx built the shipped bundle inside the floating staticappsclient:stable container with npm install, on a Node it chose itself — so the code that passed the tests and the code that shipped were different builds.

All four deploy workflows read one exact Node version from .nvmrc. The frontend moves from 20.20.2 to 22 because its pin now decides what ships. zizmor.yml keeps its own literal, which its validator needs.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The deploy target comes from the backend, and the outbound-guard follow-ups are finished
details: The deploy modal and the exported README now ask the backend which Operaton it deploys to, instead of the frontend's build-time VITE_OPERATON_BASE_URL, which is removed. A failure is not cached, so the modal names the target once the backend is reachable again.

The outbound client pins the http adapter and HTTP/1 on every request, and a refused redirect surfaces as EOUTBOUNDREFUSED. Also: the unreachable ::/128 and ::1/128 entries are removed, test-connection gets its own request schema with apiToken optional, and the credential-leak test searches the whole call.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Report-only Content-Security-Policy, SPARQL queries via the backend, and a CSP report collector (#161)
details: A Vite plugin writes staticwebapp.config.json at build time with a Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only header for the build's own backend origin, plus Reporting-Endpoints, nosniff and a referrer policy. The inline style block moves into index.css. The SPARQL editor now sends queries through POST /v1/triplydb/query instead of calling the typed endpoint and falling back to the allorigins.win proxy, so connect-src names one origin and the #142 checks apply. POST /v1/csp-reports accepts both report formats and logs each violation, storing nothing.
Also fixes the Organizations view's reversed query arguments, makes the 413 detail state the limit that applied, and handles non-JSON SPARQL error bodies.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Make the entrance animations real and keep Settings closed on full-width views (#160, #76)
details: The error banner and Settings panel used tailwindcss-animate classes, but that plugin was never installed, so both appeared instantly. Two keyframes in tailwind.config.js now provide the fade-down and slide-in-left the markup asked for, without a dependency, and motion-reduce turns them off.

Changelog, DMN Validator and SHACL Validator hide the Settings overlay because it would cover them, but its state stayed open: the gear stayed lit, clicks did nothing, and the panel reappeared on the next view. Entering those views now closes Settings, and the gear is disabled there with a tooltip saying why.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Refuse a blank title, id or name, and document running the ROPA site locally (#156)
details: The #150 checks treated only an absent or null value as missing, so an empty or whitespace-only string passed and a ROPA record could be saved with no title. A new nonBlank rule refuses that for the fields that identify or name a record: the ROPA record's title and bpmnProcessId, and the id, name and bpmnProcessId of BPMN processes, forms and documents. Other text fields may still be empty, so a ROPA draft can be saved while it is written. No stored record on local, ACC or PROD has a blank value in these fields.
The root README gains a section on running the public ROPA site on localhost (npx serve . -l 5500), and the site's own README names the port.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Keep one identity per stored process, and stop swallowing save failures (#156)
details: Saving a process now takes bpmnProcessId from the saved XML, so renaming the process id no longer leaves a stale value that makes the next deploy create a second row. The by-process-id lookup orders by deployed_at then updated_at, so a duplicate resolves to the deployed, most recently touched row. The process-id pattern requires whitespace before id= on both sides.

Also: the unrecorded-bundle reason names its actual cause; save and error banners clear on switching process; the API description no longer mentions an UPDATE; process create, import and rename and the ROPA delete report a failed write, naming the process; boardOwner is validated on the server as a lowercase slug. The unique constraint is left for #171.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Fetch DMN XML from /v1 and remove the duplicate legacy handler (#132)
details: The frontend fetched DMN XML from /api/dmns/{key}/xml without encoding the key. A separate handler, dmn-xml.routes.ts, was mounted on the app ahead of the router, so it answered every /api/dmns/:x/xml request and the /api/dmns alias never added its Deprecation and successor Link headers there.

The export now fetches /v1/dmns/{identifier}/xml with the identifier URL-encoded. The duplicate handler, its test and its mount are removed; the legacy URL is still served by the /v1 handler through the alias, now with the deprecation headers. Nothing outside this repository used the legacy path or its 404 message.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Choose any DSO authority by level instead of four fixed locations
details: The Activities tab offered four hardcoded authorities (Lelystad, Flevoland, Ede, Gelderland), so no other authority's activities could be browsed. Two dropdowns replace them: Level (gemeente, provincie, waterschap, rijk) and Authority. Options show the name without the level prefix, so typing jumps to it, and sort with 's-Hertogenbosch under H.

The list is generated from the government organisations register (organisaties.overheid.nl) by scripts/generate-dso-authorities.mjs (npm run authorities:generate): 342 municipalities, 12 provinces, 21 water boards and 12 ministries, each with its OIN. Ended organisations and those without an OIN are left out. The same list names the authority when importing forms, so any authority now gets its register name instead of a code.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: OpenAPI tidy-ups, contract scripts, and fetch every DSO activity page (#153, #148, #158)
details: POST /dso/activiteiten/oin requested one page of 200 and presented it as the whole set; Provincie Zuid-Holland has 838 activities on DSO pre, so its Activities tab filtered a partial list. The backend now fetches every page, up to 10 (2000 activities), and returns one combined list; page.size below page.totalElements signals the cap.

Also: test:contract and test:openapi-coverage scripts and a README section on adding a route; a shared ValidationSummary schema for the DMN and SHACL results, with descriptions saying the shapes match on purpose; health checks grouped under Health & monitoring; eDocs mocks using real status values; internal source names removed from the API description; the STTR example DMN regenerated with the current extraction; and a named test for the complete: false SHACL result.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Make asset status non-null and serialise every mapper's timestamps the same way (#151)
details: form_schemas.status and document_templates.status defaulted to 'wip' but were nullable, so a row written outside the upserts could reach the API as status: null, which the OpenAPI description forbids. The migration now backfills any NULL and sets the columns NOT NULL; both steps are safe on every start, and ACC and PROD hold no NULL rows today.

mapBpmn, mapForm and mapDocument now return ISO strings for createdAt and updatedAt, as mapRopaRecord already did, and the domain types say string. The wire format is unchanged, since res.json already serialised the Date the same way; the types now also match what the upserts receive.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Keep a local .env out of the outbound-target tests (#142)
details: config.ts loads .env under Jest too, so a developer with ALLOW_LOCAL_ENDPOINTS=true, the setting local Jena needs, saw 46 of the #142 tests fail. A Jest setup file now pins both #142 settings to their ACC/PROD values before any module reads .env; dotenv never overrides a variable that is already set.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Keep the outbound guard in force under an environment proxy (#142)
details: axios reads HTTP(S)_PROXY when no proxy is configured, and for https targets swaps in its own tunnelling agent, so the connect-time lookup never ran. The guarded client now pins proxy: false and strips per-request transport, socketPath and lookup overrides. Deprecated site-local fec0::/10 and Teredo 2001::/32 are refused as internal. Also: the TriplyDB service's config parameter is renamed so it no longer shadows the module config, the chain execution endpoint description says it is checked even for DRDs, and the design spec records what the implementation found.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Stop choosing the Operaton target, and hide the local endpoint preset outside development (#142)
details: The deploy modal no longer offers an Operaton URL, username or password, and names the Operaton it deploys to instead; the request stops sending those fields. The Local Jena preset appears only in development builds, where the backend admits local endpoints. The default endpoint is now chosen by URL rather than by position, so it stays DMN Discovery in every build.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Deploy processes only to the configured Operaton (#142)
details: POST /dmns/process/deploy no longer builds an Operaton client from the request. It always deploys through the shared client, which carries OPERATON_API_KEY, so Operaton credentials stay on the backend. An operatonUrl equal to the configured one is still accepted for older frontends; any other answers 400. operatonUsername and operatonPassword are ignored. All three fields are marked deprecated, and the bundle record stores the Operaton actually used.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Allowlist TriplyDB hosts that receive a token, and move the assets token to a header (#142)
details: update-service, list-graphs and test-connection forward the caller's token, so their base URL must be https and a host in TRIPLYDB_ALLOWED_HOSTS; anything else answers 400 before any request. test-connection now checks its required fields. GET /triplydb/assets reads the token from an Authorization: Bearer header instead of the apiToken query parameter, which no caller used, and encodes account and dataset into the upstream path. The frontend logo resolver sends the header.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Answer 400 for refused SPARQL endpoints (#142)
details: GET /norms, the five DMN reads, chain execution, both vendor reads, SHACL merged validation and POST /triplydb/query now check a caller-supplied endpoint before any request and answer 400 INVALID_INPUT when it is not https, carries credentials or points to an internal address. The API description documents the 400s and states the rule on each endpoint parameter, and the lint exceptions that assumed the endpoint was unvalidated are removed. The template routes and DELETE /cache/clear never request their endpoint and are unchanged.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Send caller-chosen SPARQL and TriplyDB requests through the guard (#142)
details: The SPARQL service's per-endpoint client and all five TriplyDB service calls now use the guarded outbound client. The TriplyDB calls move from fetch to axios so there is one mechanism to guard; their status handling, bodies and error messages are unchanged, and they now observe TRIPLYDB_TIMEOUT. The configured default endpoint keeps its plain client.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Refuse internal addresses when connecting to caller-chosen hosts (#142)
details: Add outboundHttp.ts: an axios client whose agents refuse a name that resolves to an internal address, whose redirects are re-checked, and whose request interceptor refuses internal IP literals and non-https URLs, which Node connects to without a DNS lookup. ALLOW_LOCAL_ENDPOINTS admits them for local development.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Check caller-supplied outbound URLs at the route (#142)
details: Add outboundUrl.ts: checks for SPARQL endpoints (any public https host), TriplyDB base URLs that carry a token (https and TRIPLYDB_ALLOWED_HOSTS), and the Operaton deploy target (only the configured one), plus the helper that answers 400 problem details. Internal addresses are recognised in every textual IPv4 and IPv6 form, including the IPv6 forms that embed an IPv4 address and trailing-dot localhost names. ALLOW_LOCAL_ENDPOINTS admits http and local addresses for development.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Plan outbound target validation (#142)
details: The eight-task implementation plan for #142 that the outbound-target commits below follow.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Design outbound target validation (#142)
details: The design for issue #142: which caller-supplied targets the backend may call, checked at the route and again when the connection opens, and why the Operaton deploy target is pinned.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Correct the public ROPA site's hosts and local setup
details: The error-contract plan listed the public ROPA site as an unchecked consumer under ropa.flevoland.nl, a name taken from a stale comment in publicPaths.ts. That host does not resolve. The site is packages/ropa-site, served at ropa.open-regels.nl and acc.ropa.open-regels.nl, and it never reads an error body.

Correct the plan's known-risk section and the comment, and rewrite the site's README: its real hosts, which backend each host talks to, the two deploy workflows, and that opening index.html from disk talks to the production backend.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Switch the problem-details lint rules on (#131)
details: Every error response the API produces itself is now problem details, so nlgov:use-problem-schema and nlgov:problem-schema-members gate the whole document instead of being switched off. Two responses stay exempt, each at the one response it concerns: the evaluate proxy's 500, which forwards Operaton's own body, and GET /health's 503, which is the health document itself. Removing either exemption makes exactly that response fail.

The design spec said these rules were off pending #131, that the Assets exception would disappear when #150 landed, and counted nine DSO exceptions. It now records what happened: the rules gate, the Assets exception shrank to five entries for a reason that is a design choice rather than a defect, and two DSO entries left when a malformed body became a 400.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Validate input on the asset and ROPA routes (#150)
details: A missing field, an unknown status or a malformed id reached Postgres and came back as a 500, so a caller could not tell a mistake in its request from a server failure. The four upserts, the deploy mark and the ROPA delete now check their input first and answer 400 INVALID_INPUT, with a detail naming every field that failed.

The checks follow the database's own constraints: presence where a column is NOT NULL and the handler supplies no fallback, type where a value is bound, and enum where a column has a CHECK. Form and document status have no CHECK, so any string passes. XML and JSON blobs are checked for presence and type only and never parsed. DELETE /assets/ropa/{id} checks the id is a UUID before it reaches a query that would fail the cast.

In a few edge cases the checks are deliberately stricter than Postgres, which would coerce or store the string "1" for an integer, "true" for a boolean, or JSON null for a required JSON value. No client sends these and storing them would leave rows no reader expects. The frontend's own payloads were checked at every call site, sent live against a running backend, and every row in a development database and every example .form and .document file in the repository was re-shaped as the frontend re-posts it; none is rejected. Integer columns now reject a fraction, which used to pass a number check and then fail as a 500.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Answer 400 and 413 for unparsable and oversized bodies (#143)
details: The global error handler answered every body-parser failure with a 500, telling a client that sent a broken or oversized body that the server had failed. It now honours the status body-parser already gives its own errors: 400 MALFORMED_BODY for a body that does not parse, 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE for one over the 10 MB limit, whose detail names the limit, and the parser's own status as INVALID_BODY for the rest, such as an unsupported charset or a urlencoded body nested past qs's depth limit.

A body-parser error is recognised by its type, against a fixed list read from the installed body-parser and raw-body. A status property alone decides nothing, so an arbitrary thrown error carrying one still answers 500 rather than choosing its own response. The limit now lives in one constant shared by the parsers and the 413 message.

The 23 operations that take a body document both responses, and the 500 descriptions no longer claim the malformed-body case. The parser runs for every method, so a body sent to a GET or DELETE gets the same answers; that is said once in info.description rather than on the ~43 operations that take no body, since such a body is outside their contract.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Answer errors as RFC 9457 problem details (#131)
details: Every error the API produces itself is now application/problem+json with status, title, detail and instance, replacing five different envelopes: { success, error: { code, message } } on most routes, a bare-string error on /dso and /vendors, TriplyDB's shape with its own status, a message-only 503 on the TriplyDB connection test, and a chain failure nested under data.error.

code survives as an extension member, since the design rules allow extra members and it is what existing callers branch on. type is about:blank: there is no documentation page per kind of problem, and a URL that does not resolve would be worse than none. instance is the request path without its query string, taken from originalUrl because a nested router rewrites req.path.
A failed chain execution keeps its partial result under data, beside the problem that describes the failure, so which steps ran and the outputs so far are not lost.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Plan the error contract pass (#131, #143, #150)
details: The plan for one pass over #131, #143 and #150, which all change what an error response looks like, so that responses are written once in the new format.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Generate Tailwind at build time instead of loading the CDN
details: index.html loaded Tailwind's Play CDN on every page load, in acceptance and production. That is third-party JavaScript executing in the application's origin with full DOM access, on an unversioned URL that cannot be pinned with an integrity hash, with no Content-Security-Policy to contain it and nothing in the supply-chain pipeline covering a script tag in HTML. Tailwind documents the Play CDN as a development tool. The styling of every screen depended on it: if the CDN were slow, blocked or serving something else, the app rendered unstyled or ran someone else's code.

Tailwind now builds with the application: tailwindcss 3.4, PostCSS and autoprefixer as build dependencies, an entry stylesheet imported from main.tsx, and a content scan over index.html and the source. Staying on v3 keeps every class meaning identical to what the CDN served; v4 would have turned a supply-chain fix into a redesign.

index.html also carried an import map naming six packages on esm.sh with floating ranges. Nothing referenced it — react is bundled, and one of the named packages is used by no source file — so it was inert, but it was a supply-chain path with no lockfile behind it, waiting for the first runtime bare import to make it live. Removed.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Record the bundle when a process is deployed
details: A deploy could report success while nothing reached Postgres. The write was a second request the browser made after the deploy, unawaited, its failure swallowed, and skipped entirely when the browser had no matching identifier in local storage. Underneath it, markDeployed reported success even when its UPDATE matched no rows. Both the caseworker dashboard and the public site list bundles by their deployment timestamp, so a process that failed to record was invisible everywhere, and nobody was told.

The deploy route now records the bundle itself. After Operaton accepts the deployment, the backend finds the stored process by the id in the BPMN, or creates a minimal row when none exists, and stamps it. The browser makes one request, and the identifier in local storage no longer decides whether a deploy is remembered.

Recording cannot fail the deploy, which already happened and cannot be undone. commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Warn that CORS_ORIGIN app settings replace rather than append (#145)
details: The comment added with the #145 fix showed the app-setting command with a literal "..." standing in for the current allowlist. That reads as an abbreviation rather than as a warning, and `az webapp config appsettings set` replaces the whole value rather than appending to it, so running the line as written -- or reconstructing the list from the local default below it -- drops every origin it does not name.

Reading the acceptance value while applying the documentation-site origins showed the hazard is worse than assumed. The deployed acceptance list held four origins, not the eight in this file, and one of them -- https://acc.cpsv-editor.open-regels.nl -- appears nowhere in the repository. It is not in .env.example, not in any workflow, and there is no Bicep, Terraform or ARM to hold it; none of the azure-*.yml workflows sets app settings at all. Each App Service application setting is therefore the only copy of its own allowlist, and this file is a local development list that was never a template for the deployed tiers.

The comment now says so, and gives the read-then-write form that cannot retype the value, with a guard refusing to write when the read comes back empty. Losing an origin this way is silent -- no error, no failing test, just a partner site whose browser calls stop working.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Refuse a disallowed CORS origin without a 500 (#145)
details: The origin callback passed an Error for any unlisted origin. The cors package treats a non-null first argument as a middleware failure and forwards it to next(err), so a request from an unrecognised origin reached the error handler and was answered with the standard INTERNAL_ERROR envelope -- a server error implying the backend had broken, when nothing had. The same options object backs app.options('*'), so preflight requests failed the same way, which is why an embedded Scalar reference on the IOU architecture documentation site could only report "Failed to fetch".

The conventional rejection is callback(null, false): emit no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header, let the request complete normally, and let the browser enforce the policy. The caller then sees an ordinary response it is not permitted to read.

Testing the wiring meant extracting it first. index.ts self-executes startServer() at module scope, so importing it in a test would run migrations and bind a port; the CORS configuration moves verbatim to middleware/cors.middleware.ts, nosemgrep annotation intact, before any behaviour changes. As a side effect the two cors() instances are now built once at module load rather than on every request.

commits.subject: Check the GitLab mirror at each release
details: Every gate in docs/the-gate-has-teeth.md runs on GitHub Actions. The gitlab remote is outside all of them and is pushed by hand, so it drifts on every merge -- and a mirror nothing checks is not a backup, it is a second place for content to be. This one had drifted 114 commits behind on acc and 253 on main before its last reconciliation.

It cannot run in CI, and that is a property of the mirror rather than a shortcoming here: the gitlab remote lives in .git/config and no tracked file names the host, so an Actions runner has no such remote, no key for it and no route to it. The check runs where the push happens, called from bump-release step 7.
It never pushes. It prints the exact command and stops, because writing to a shared remote is a human's decision.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Record RONL Business API's promotion in the cross-repo posture
details: RBA promoted acc to production on 12 September, the first deploy since 17 July, which closes three of its rows here and opens four others. Build provenance is now exercised in a third repository and a fourth surface. Its main gained a promotion-gate ruleset that reported BLOCKED on the promotion pull request, answering section 4's question the opposite way to ttl-editor. Its mirror turned out to be the dull case, both branches strict ancestors, so two fast-forwards rather than ttl-editor's surgery. Adds the newline-in-secret trap beside the pinning material: a stored credential cannot be read back, so nothing in review or in a log can show it differs by one invisible byte.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Record ttl-editor's lockfile fix, and make this page the only copy
details: This page is now the single documented source for ttl-editor and Linked Data Explorer. Each repository used to carry its own copy, and the two drifted in both directions; ttl-editor's is deleted in sgort/ttl-editor#136, and its README points here. The page now says so at the top.
It also still described ttl-editor as it was before today's fix there.

- "Seven findings remain ... cannot be closed by a Renovate bump, only by an upstream release or an overrides entry". Wrong, and now corrected: each of brace-expansion, picomatch and postcss-selector-parser had a newer version inside its declared range, and nothing had moved them because ttl-editor had no lock-file maintenance. Its first refresh, ttl-editor#135, took them to 1.1.18, 2.3.2 and 6.1.4 and the scan on acc to 0 findings. The trajectory table gains that last row, and the triage summary no longer ends at 7. - The paragraph that flagged the missing lockFileMaintenance and left it untouched now records what was checked and done: the in-range refresh and scan run in a scratch worktree first, predicting 7 to 0; ttl-editor#134 enabling it with the same two safeguards as here; and #135 delivering exactly the predicted versions, 202 packages, none within the cooldown. It also says why ttl-editor needed neither of this repository's other two fixes. - The open-work row for it is removed, and ttl-editor's verified head moves to c4a8585.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Major dependency updates wait for approval, so the lockfile refresh gets a slot
details: Major updates now wait in the Dependency Dashboard as checkboxes and hold no slot in Renovate's concurrency limit until someone approves one. The queue that kept crowding out lock-file maintenance was almost entirely majors — npm 12 and two workspace major groups spanning express, eslint, jest, typescript, vite and tiptap — which are never merged on autopilot anyway.

Giving lock-file maintenance priority alone had not been enough: it only orders branches eligible in the same run, and lock-file maintenance is eligible only inside its Monday schedule, so updates eligible any day filled every free slot first. Security fixes are exempt from the new approval step, so one that happens to be a major version never waits on a click.

commits.author: renovate[bot]
commits.subject: Backend dependency updates
details: axios 1.20.0 and @types/n3 1.26.2. Rebased onto the current tree before merging, so its lockfile was regenerated against the refreshed dependencies rather than the January ones, and verified locally with lint, the full test suite and the backend build.

commits.author: renovate[bot]
commits.subject: Frontend dependency updates
