commits.author: renovate[bot]
commits.subject: Workflow Node versions pinned to exact patches
details: The floating majors in the deployment workflows are pinned: 20.20.2 for the frontend, 22.23.2 for the backend, 24.19.0 for the supply-chain audit.

commits.author: renovate[bot]
commits.subject: lint-staged updated to ^16.4.0

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Deploy refuses a bundle whose forms or documents are missing from local storage
details: The deploy modal filtered referenced forms and document templates against the browser’s own storage and dropped every miss without a word, so a bundle could deploy with none of its .document resources and still show a green "Resources to deploy" panel.

The failure surfaced far from its cause. RipR21Process deployed with its BPMN and twelve forms but none of its three documents; at runtime ronl-business-api read ronl:signatureRef from the engine, looked for rip-pdp.document in the deployment, threw SIGNATURE_TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND and returned 500 from the task spec endpoint. ProjectDetail fetches that spec inside a Promise.allSettled and degrades a failure to "no signature required", so the phase-exit approval task rendered an ordinary form instead of the signing panel and the E2E journey failed on a missing panel.

Missing resources are now listed by name and the deploy button is disabled while any remain, matching the existing board-owner and organization guards. unmatchedForms was already computed but rendered nowhere, and is surfaced alongside it. extractDocumentRefs now also follows ronl:signatureRef: a task binding a template through that attribute alone never contributed it, and rip-pdp survived only because it carries both. No bundle in the repository changes as a result. The resources footer, which printed its count twice with the first total omitting documents, is collapsed to one.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Forms bind to their own deployment instead of the latest version
details: Tenanting a process definition made the process unambiguous and its forms ambiguous. camunda:formRefBinding="latest" resolves a form key across the whole repository rather than within the bundle, so deploying AwbShellProcess under tenant flevoland produced ENGINE-03109: the key ‘kapvergunning-start’ existed for multiple tenants. "deployment" resolves the form from the process definition’s own deployment, unique by construction, so tenanted and untenanted copies coexist and no deployment history has to be destroyed.

91 of 109 references converted across the three trees that hold BPMN: packages/frontend/public/examples/ (seed and deploy source for the Awb/Zorgtoeslag/DvTP/HR bundles), examples/organizations/ (authoring source for RIP and HR-capacity), and e2e-fixtures/ (what ronl-business-api’s E2E suite deploys). thuisbatterij and ind stay on "latest" because their form keys resolve nowhere in the repository.

Also bumps the seven seeded BPMN entries in EXAMPLE_VERSIONS. public/examples is seeded into localStorage and re-fetched only when its version rises, so without the bump the edit would be invisible to every existing user. Already-deployed definitions do not heal: ACC users get the fix only after a frontend deploy and a page load that re-seeds, and the e2e-fixtures bundles must be re-imported through the BPMN Modeler before an E2E run exercises them.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Changelog gains the ci and repo scope tags
details: The scope field offered frontend, backend and both. Three entries in this release change no deployable's code at all, so none of the three was true for them.

'ci' covers pipeline and supply-chain work and mirrors the tag ronl-business-api already uses, so both repositories label the same kind of work the same way. 'repo' covers everything else that ships no application code: documentation, and the Operaton deploy bundles under examples/ and e2e-fixtures/. Those bundles are worth distinguishing from a frontend change, because the frontend serves its own copies from packages/frontend/public/examples/ - the root directories are read only by the backend's tests and deployed to Operaton separately.
Labelling any of it 'both' would have told a reader that a release touching only .github/ had changed application code.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: bump-release lands through a pull request and reconciles Renovate first
details: Two steps of the command were not merely out of date but impossible. Step 7 fast-forwarded acc locally and asked separately about pushing; both halves are now rejected, because acc requires a pull request and a passing audit check. It is rewritten to push the branch, open a pull request, and let a human merge it - merging is the push.

The merge method is called out because both alternatives silently break the entry: it names every commit by SHA, and squash collapses them into one new commit while rebase replays them as new commits, preserving the count while replacing every hash.

Step 0 is new. Renovate raises dependency pull requests continuously and they rewrite package-lock.json, the same file the version bump edits. Three lessons from this release are recorded: verify each one locally because no pull-request check runs backend tests, include check-format because it runs in no workflow at all, and trial-merge a stale branch before trusting a clean-looking result.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Changelog renders the ci type, and an unknown scope no longer crashes the panel
details: The commit-type union had no 'ci'. Unknown types fall back to 'other', so a ci entry would have rendered rather than crashed - but as a generic document icon, filing an entire supply-chain effort under "other". It now has its own icon and colour, distinct from chore.

ScopeBadge had no such fallback. changelog.json is imported as untyped JSON and cast at the module boundary, so TypeScript never checks the scope strings the data actually carries; an unrecognised one reached SCOPE_BADGE[scope], yielded undefined, and would take the whole panel down on config.cls. The type system cannot help here by construction, so the guard is the only thing that can - and it is what makes the scope tags added next safe to introduce.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Reformatted for prettier 3.9
details: Prettier 3.9 formats short union types on a single line rather than the leading-pipe multiline style 3.7 produced, leaving five existing files failing prettier --check the moment the upgrade landed.

No workflow runs check-format - the deploy workflows run lint and tests only - so nothing in CI reported it. The gate that catches this is the pre-push hook, which means the symptom would have been the next person's push failing on files they never touched.

commits.author: renovate[bot]
commits.subject: Backend dependencies brought up to date
details: Twenty-three packages, of which exactly one carried an advisory: express 4.18.2 to 4.22.2. The rest - helmet, pg, winston, dotenv, cors, sparql-http-client and the TypeScript, ESLint and Jest toolchain - are routine currency rather than security work, and are recorded as such rather than presented as advisory fixes.

Two had consequences beyond their own version. prettier 3.9.6 reformatted five untouched files, and typescript 5.9.3 warranted a full build to verify. Both were checked before the merge, because the backend workflow runs no tests on a pull request.

commits.author: renovate[bot]
commits.subject: fast-xml-parser advisory closed
details: Range raised from ^5.3.5 to ^5.7.0, the minimum patched release, with the lockfile resolving to 5.11.1. That split is rangeStrategy bump working as intended: raise the floor to the safe version, let the lockfile pin the current one.
Raised through the vulnerabilityAlerts fast-lane, which clears the 14-day cooldown for known advisories - the one class of update that must not wait.

commits.author: renovate[bot]
commits.subject: axios advisory closed
details: Range raised from ^1.6.5 to ^1.18.0 with the lockfile resolving to 1.20.0, spanning fourteen minor releases - the widest jump in this release.

Verified against the full backend suite locally before merging, since the backend deploy workflow triggers on push only and the sole pull-request check says nothing about whether a dependency broke anything.

commits.author: renovate[bot]
commits.subject: concurrently updated
details: Root devDependency, no advisory. Its branch was never rebased because it did not conflict, so the merge was trialled locally first and the resulting lockfile checked with npm ci - a clean textual merge of two lockfile diffs can still produce a file npm will not accept.

commits.author: renovate[bot]
commits.subject: vite advisory closed
details: Frontend build tooling raised from ^6.2.0 to ^6.4.3.

The only one of the three security updates whose pull request ran the full lint, test and preview-deploy chain, because the frontend workflow triggers on pull requests and the backend workflow does not - the asymmetry that made local verification necessary for the other two.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Config validator runs on the Node version Renovate requires
details: renovate 44.50.3 declares engines.node ^24.11.0 and the runner defaults to Node 22. npm accepts the mismatch with an EBADENGINE warning rather than refusing, so the validator ran unsupported and still reported green - the kind of mismatch that keeps working right up until a release stops tolerating it.

setup-node is placed before the zizmor step rather than beside the validator it serves. A step following a failed one is skipped, so putting it after would mean the validator's if: always() ran on whatever Node the runner defaulted to, precisely when zizmor had already failed and the logs were being read.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: renovate.json validated by the audit gate
details: The gate caught every floating action reference and had nothing to say about a malformed renovate.json - which is how five invalid "//" keys reached acc and stopped Renovate opening any pull request at all. Pins without updates decay into an unpatched tree, so a silently inert Renovate is a supply-chain failure the audit exists to prevent.

renovate-config-validator runs as a second step in the same audit job, so it is covered by the existing required status check and needs no ruleset change. It runs with no filename argument, because passing one switches the validator into global config mode and applies different rules, and under if: always() so a zizmor failure cannot hide a broken configuration behind it.

--strict earned its place immediately. It fails on configuration Renovate would auto-migrate rather than reject, which surfaced baseBranches - renamed upstream to baseBranchPatterns, silently migrated on every run, and therefore invisible.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Renovate configuration comments moved to description fields
details: Renovate validates strictly and rejects unknown options, so the "//"-prefixed keys used as JSON comments were read as five invalid settings rather than ignored. Renovate stopped opening pull requests as a precaution - correct behaviour from it, but it meant the half of the supply-chain policy that keeps pins current was inert from the moment it landed.

Every comment moves to a description field, valid at the top level and inside any nested object. No policy changes: the cooldown, the security fast-lane, the workspace groups and the static-web-apps-deploy exclusion are identical in effect; only the annotation style differs.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Supply-chain pinning enforced on the acceptance pipeline
details: Nothing downloaded or executed by this pipeline may float. All twenty action references across the six deployment workflows are now commit hashes with their version in a trailing comment, and a zizmor gate refuses any pull request that reintroduces a floating tag. Findings go from 40 to 0.

Each workflow also gains the hardening zizmor was reporting: persist-credentials false on checkout, explicit workflow and job permissions, and a concurrency group keyed on the pull-request number rather than the ref - because github.ref alone puts the pull_request(closed) teardown and the push deploy that a merge fires into one group, where they cancel each other at random.

renovate.json supplies the other half of the policy: a 14-day cooldown with internalChecksFilter strict, cleared by vulnerabilityAlerts for known advisories, and dependencies grouped per workspace. SECURITY-PIPELINE.md records what is pinned and, more importantly, what is not - the static-web-apps-deploy Docker image behind four workflows, and the backend deploy step's lockfile-less npm install.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: ValidSign signature mirrored into the R2.1 examples copy
details: RipR21Process.bpmn exists in two places the parity test locks together byte for byte: examples/organizations/flevoland/rip-phase-21/ is the authored source, e2e-fixtures/flevoland/ is the mirror. The signature attribute had been added to the mirror only, so the two had drifted apart.

The parity test had been failing since the signature commit. Because the backend deploy workflow triggers on push only, no pull request runs these tests - the failure would have surfaced on acc after merge, where npm test gates the deploy step, leaving a red acceptance branch and no deployment.
The xmlns:ronl namespace was already declared in both files and the byte delta was exactly the length of the attribute, so this adds one attribute rather than reflowing the document.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: ValidSign signature required on the R2.1 phase-exit approval
details: Adds ronl:signatureRef="rip-pdp" to Task_AccorderenProjectplan4, the "Accorderen Projectplan 4. Uitgangspunten VO-fase" task that closes R2.1.

This one attribute is the switch for the whole signing feature built in ronl-business-api. The backend resolves ronl:signatureRef on a user task and, when present, replaces that task's plain approval form with a ValidSign signing ceremony: the phase document is rendered from its deployed template, a signature package is created, and the Operaton task completes only once the signature lands.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Dutch grammar corrected in the join-gateway annotation
details: "het pool" becomes "de pool" - pool is common-gender - and the subordinate clause was missing "dat": the source PDF shows THAT the two branches leave the pool, not the branches themselves.
Text only, and both copies were updated together so the parity test stayed green.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Final review findings on the R2.2 bundle addressed
details: Four findings from the whole-branch review. The notable one was a dangling SHA: 39a49bb survived only on a sibling branch slated for deletion, so citing it in the parity test's doc comment, a changelog entry and three places in the planning document would have left references that stop resolving.
Replaced throughout with 49832d2 - the same reachable commit with the same meaning, the one that repaired the document zone keys in the e2e-fixtures copies.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Changelog entry for the R2.2 VO bundle
details: Records the RipR22Process bundle, the rip-phase1-swimlanes to rip-phase-21 rename, and the parity test now holding the examples/ and e2e-fixtures/ copies of each bundle together.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Five R2.2 document templates added — KES, Ontwerptoelichting, Objectenboom, Bevindingenformulier, Hoeveelheidsbepaling
details: One template per green “Format …” box in R2_2 - VO.pdf: KES, Ontwerptoelichting, Objectenboom, Bevindingenformulier and Hoeveelheidsbepaling. A Format in the diagram and a `.document` in LDE are the same thing — a template with bindings — so the mapping is direct; the blue outputs beside them in the spec are instances of these templates rather than artifacts of their own.

Zone keys are `signOff` and `contactInformation`, camelCase, from the start — unlike R2.1's templates, which shipped with `signoff` and `contactInfo`, keys `DocumentZones` never declares, leaving their signature blocks unrendered until 49832d2 repaired them.
Completes the RipR22Process bundle: the manifest now declares nothing that does not exist, and the fixture suite is green.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Nine R2.2 user task forms added, one per lane task, bound by camunda:formRef
details: One form per user task in RipR22Process. Field types stay inside the eight the R2.1 bundle already uses — text, textarea, textfield, checkbox, datetime, select, radio, button — since nothing else is exercised against this Camunda 7.21 stack.

The spec's conditional “LCC-raming (indien variantenafweging)” is modelled as a checkbox plus a reference field on `rip-concept-vo.form` rather than an artifact of its own, since it only exists when a variant trade-off happened.

`klicMeldingReferentie` is collected only on `rip-inventariseren-kabels-leidingen.form`. The concept VO task reads the same information but does not also write it, since two forms writing one process variable would mean whichever task completes last silently wins.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: R2.2 document templates were unattached — RipR22Process shipped without ronl:documentRef
details: R2.1 wires each document template to the task that produces it with `ronl:documentRef` — the attribute `DocumentTemplateSelector` writes and `BpmnCanvas` reads to render the document badge on a task in the Modeler. The R2.2 spec never mentioned it, so RipR22Process shipped without it and the five templates added alongside it would have imported but attached to nothing.

The attribute is single-valued, so a task can carry at most one template. Four of the five bind: Task_VerzamelenKlanteisen → rip-kes, Task_OpstellenConceptVO → rip-ontwerptoelichting, Task_BesprekenConceptVO → rip-bevindingenformulier, Task_OpstellenDefinitiefVO → rip-hoeveelheidsbepaling. `rip-objectenboom` stays unattached on purpose — Task_OpstellenConceptVO produces both the Ontwerptoelichting and the Objectenboom, and its one slot went to the Ontwerptoelichting; the Objectenboom still ships and imports normally, it simply carries no task badge. Its reference is additionally maintained in Relatics.
Values are bare template ids with no `.document` suffix, matching R2.1. Both the `examples/` and `e2e-fixtures/` copies are updated so the parity test stays green.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: RipR22Process added — four lanes, nine user tasks, from R2_2 - VO.pdf
details: Four lanes and nine user tasks from R2_2 - VO.pdf (rev. 21-11-2024), picking up where RipR21Process's “Fase 1 voltooid → R2.2” end event left off.

All five branches of the opening parallel split rejoin the join gateway. The PDF does not draw it that way — it shows Inventariseren kabels en leidingen and Aanvragen raamvergunning leaving the pool into CO1 and JU3.5 and never coming back, which as control flow deadlocks at the join. Those hand-offs are `textAnnotation`s instead: CO1 and JU3.5 do not exist as fixtures, so a `callActivity` would dangle at deploy time and fail the manifest's `calledElement` test. They are referenced by several phases and belong in a shared bundle of their own.
The manifest entry declares the nine forms and five documents that the following commits add, so the fixture suite's file-existence test stays red until the bundle is complete.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: New parity test locks each RIP bundle's examples/ and e2e-fixtures/ copies together
details: Each RIP bundle exists twice on disk: authored under `examples/`, imported and deployed from `e2e-fixtures/`. Nothing stopped the two drifting, and they have — 49832d2 repaired the document zone keys in the `e2e-fixtures` copies only, and the `examples` copies kept the dead `signoff`/`contactInfo` keys until 44d1cb4 re-pasted them by hand.
A new test asserts every file in a mirrored bundle is byte-identical to its twin. New bundles opt in by adding an entry to `MIRRORED_BUNDLES`.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: rip-phase1-swimlanes renamed to rip-phase-21
details: The `-swimlanes` suffix distinguished this bundle from a competing `rip-phase1/` draft that b1b88a8 deleted, so it now distinguishes nothing, and the directory name no longer matched the process it holds (RipR21Process). Renaming it makes the incoming R2.2 bundle an obvious sibling: `rip-phase-21/` holds RipR21Process, `rip-phase-22/` holds RipR22Process.

Contents are untouched. Exactly one reference to the old path existed — the `source` field of the RipR21Process entry in `e2e-fixtures/manifest.json` — and it is repointed here. Nothing resolves this directory at runtime; the app serves examples from `packages/frontend/public/examples/`, which has never held the RIP bundles.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Implementation plan for the R2.2 VO deploy bundle
details: Six tasks: rename rip-phase1-swimlanes to rip-phase-21, add a parity test, then the BPMN, the nine forms and the five documents, closing with the changelog and a full verification pass.

Task 3 declares all fifteen files in the manifest up front, so the fixture suite's file-existence test stays red through Tasks 3 and 4 and turns green only at the end of Task 5. The plan flags that as the expected state, so nobody "fixes" it by trimming the manifest back.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Design for the RipR22Process (R2.2 - VO) deploy bundle
details: Turns the R2_2 - VO source PDF (rev. 21-11-2024) into a specification for a bundle LDE can import and deploy: a four-lane BPMN process with nine user tasks, nine Camunda form-js forms, and five document templates - one per green "Format" in the diagram, since a Format there and a .document here are the same thing.
Flags the design decisions worth knowing later, including that the cross-phase hand-offs to CO1 and JU3.5 are text annotations rather than modelled flows.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Fixture repairs rebased onto the current examples
details: Housekeeping commit carrying the repaired RIP document templates into their final position alongside the R2.1 examples.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Signature blocks and process key repaired in the RIP document templates
details: Two defects had shipped with every deployment of the three RIP document templates in e2e-fixtures/flevoland.

The templates used "signoff" and "contactInfo" where DocumentZones declares "signOff" and "contactInformation". DocumentCanvas iterates ZONE_ORDER and calls getZoneBlocks('signOff'), so the lowercase key meant the Signatures block was dropped silently - the three signature lines in these templates had never rendered.
They also declared processKey "RipPhase1Process" while the BPMN they deploy with declares RipR21Process, which is also the key the fixture manifest lists them under.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: R2.1 examples rebased against the e2e fixtures
details: Brings the authored examples/ copies back in line with the e2e-fixtures/ mirror, ahead of the parity test that would later enforce it mechanically.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Child-activity fan-out in the Activity Detail panel documented
details: The RTR returns onderliggendeActiviteiten as bare HAL hrefs with no omschrijving, so ActivityDetailPanel fires one extra activity-detail request per child, in parallel, purely to resolve names. Opening a single activity therefore costs 1 + N upstream RTR calls - 24 for an activity with 23 children.

Records the call shape, the Promise.allSettled error isolation, the name-or-URN fallback, and the absence of any cache or concurrency cap. Flagged as the viewer's heaviest interaction and the first candidate for memoisation.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Every DSO API behind the DSO Viewer documented
details: Maps each DSO Viewer feature to the upstream API behind it: Stelselcatalogus v3 for concepts, RTR Gegevens v2 for activities, Zoekinterface v2 for werkzaamheden search, Opvragen Werkzaamheden v1 for werkzaamheid detail, and Toepasbare Regels Uitvoeren Gegevens v1 for rule metadata.

Includes the UI to LDE to DSO call path per feature, a complete endpoint map, pre and prod base URLs and env vars, and transport conventions. Notes that the geo point search is implemented and tested but not yet wired into the UI, and that /toepasbare-regels/:id/dmn is a contract shared with the CPSV Editor.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Lockfile synchronised with the current package versions
details: Routine reconciliation after a pull and install, so the lockfile stops carrying a stale resolution set into the next change.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: bump-release now versions the lockfile, not just package.json
details: The release step said “set `version` in each in-scope package.json” and nothing more, so no release ever touched `package-lock.json`. Through v2026.08.2 it still recorded the root at `1.9.13` and `packages/backend` at `0.1.0`, while every `package.json` in the repo had reached `2026.08.2`.

The step now uses `npm version <ver> --no-git-tag-version`, once for the root and once per in-scope workspace, which writes each `package.json` and its lockfile entry together. The drift was never fatal — `npm ci` validates dependency satisfiability, and the root depends on its workspaces by path rather than by version range, so those `version` fields are never checked — but the lockfile is what CI installs from and what SBOM, audit and provenance tooling reads, so all of it reported the wrong versions.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: E2E fixture BPMNs were undeployable — artifacts placed before flow elements
details: BPMN 2.0’s `tProcess` is an ordered sequence — `laneSet*`, `flowElement*`, `artifact*`, `resourceRole*`, `correlationSubscription*`, `supports*` — so once an artifact appears, no further flow element may follow it. Operaton validates against the XSD on deploy and rejects the entire deployment when it doesn’t hold, with `cvc-complex-type.2.4.a: Invalid content was found starting with element '{…}:scriptTask'`.

The commit that added the on-canvas “E2E FIXTURE” warning inserted its `textAnnotation` and `association` directly after the first flow element, leaving four of the five fixtures undeployable. Each banner moves to just before `</bpmn:process>`, matching `TreeFellingPermitSubProcessE2E` — the one file that had it right and the only one that deployed. A pure move: no content changes, DI untouched, and all five now validate against `bpmn-moddle`’s `BPMN20.xsd`.

Nothing caught this because the integrity test checked file existence, process ids and `calledElement` references but never whether the BPMN was deployable at all. These fixtures are hand-edited and never round-trip through bpmn-js, which would have re-serialised them into schema order and silently repaired the mistake. A fifth test now asserts the ordering rule directly.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: BPMN process key was always the literal string “process”
details: `doc.querySelector('process')` is a CSS *type* selector, which matches only the null namespace — so it never found the `<bpmn:process>` element that real bpmn-js output always emits, and all four call sites in `BpmnCanvas` fell through to their own fallbacks every time. Every deployment posted `“process”` as its process key instead of the model’s actual id, and sub-process lookups by `calledElement` never matched.

A new `findProcessElement` helper uses `getElementsByTagNameNS` to match on local name across namespaces, and all four call sites route through it. The test covering this had asserted the fallback as correct, attributing it to a jsdom quirk — that reading was half right: the fixture behind it declared none of the prefixes it used, so `DOMParser` rejected the document outright and returned a `<parsererror>` in which nothing was findable under any lookup, masking the real defect underneath.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Error overlay was unreachable from the view that raised it
details: The overlay lived inside `App`’s right panel, which is hidden whenever `viewMode` is Orchestration, BPMN, Form, Document, ROPA, DSO or either validator. `handleRefreshCache` can only be triggered from Orchestration, so a failed cache clear set the error state correctly and then had nowhere to render — silent until the user happened to navigate elsewhere, where a stale error appeared out of context.

The overlay is now a direct child of the workspace container, which is already positioned relative, so it renders in every view. `App.test.tsx` previously asserted the broken behaviour explicitly; it now asserts the error appears on the view that caused it and is dismissible there.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Every deploy now gated on lint and the test suite
details: None of the six Azure workflows ran a test step, blocking or otherwise. That was a deliberate P7 decision taken when backend coverage was first measured at 13.82% statements — gating on a number that low would have been theatre — recorded as conditional on backend breadth improving. v2026.08.2 took the backend from 16.79% to 98.06%, meeting the condition.

The backend workflows already installed and linted, so the test step slots in beside the existing `npm run lint`. The frontend workflows had no npm steps at all, because the Static Web Apps action builds inside its own container and runs none of this repository’s scripts; they gain an explicit install, lint and test sequence ahead of the deploy action. The two `ropa-site` workflows are deliberately untouched — that package is a static `index.html` with no build and no test script to run.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Repo-side test documentation retired in favour of the documentation site
details: Deletes `docs/TESTS.md` (982 lines) and `docs/TESTING-GUIDE.md` (228 lines). The IOU Architecture documentation site is now the single source of truth for test documentation, at `linked-data-explorer/developer/testing`; the repo-side copies had drifted from what the suites actually do and are not maintained.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: lint-staged skipped backend files at pre-commit
details: Companion to the `check-format` fix below — the same blind spot, one stage earlier. `lint-staged` was configured with a single glob for `packages/frontend/**`, so committing a backend file ran neither Prettier nor ESLint over it.

Adds `packages/backend/src/**/*.ts` with the backend’s own `eslint.config.js`. The scope is deliberately `src/**/*.ts` rather than the whole package: that is exactly what the backend’s `check-format` gates, so pre-commit and pre-push now agree rather than one rewriting files the other never checks.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Root check-format silently skipped the backend
details: The two workspaces named their Prettier check differently — backend `format:check`, frontend `check-format` — while the root script runs `npm run check-format --workspaces --if-present`. Because `--if-present` skips a missing script rather than failing, the backend was quietly dropped from every root `check-format` run.

`.husky/pre-push` runs exactly that root script, so backend formatting was never actually gated on push. The gap was silent in both directions: the root command exited 0, and its output listed only the frontend. The backend now defines `check-format` as its canonical name, with `format:check` retained as an alias.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: "years and months duration(...)" built-in name false-flagged as an unresolved variable (INT-007)
details: FEEL_RESERVED had the singular year/month/day/hour/minute/second (for year(...)/month(...) single-word built-ins) but not the plural years/months -- the two words of the "years and months duration(...)" built-in's own name. Its leading words aren't preceded by a dot, so only the reserved-word check catches them; the pre-existing dot-check already handled the trailing .years/.months property access on the duration result correctly.

Reproduced live against HvA_full_dmn_export-patched.dmn: 12 INT-007 warnings across 6 decisions, all false positives from this exact construct (e.g. "(years and months duration(npGeboortedatum, peildatum)).years").

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: POST /v1/dmns/evaluate/:decisionKey -- raw passthrough evaluate proxy
details: The CPSV Editor's DMN tab called Operaton's evaluate endpoint directly from the browser, which CORS blocks for a local dev origin. This route proxies the call server-side instead, forwarding Operaton's response byte-for-byte and status-for-status (success array or exception object) rather than the usual {success, data, error} envelope, since the DMN tab reads Operaton's raw JSON directly.

New evaluateRaw() on operatonService passes variables straight through, without the plain-JS-value type inference evaluateDecision() does for its own (different) caller contract -- the DMN tab already constructs Operaton-shaped request bodies itself, so re-wrapping them would double-wrap and break the request.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: POST /v1/dmns/deploy -- ad-hoc raw DMN XML deploy
details: Deploys DMN content directly, without requiring pre-registered LDE norm identifiers first -- built for the CPSV Editor's DMN tab, which has an uploaded/generated DMN file with no registry entry of its own. A thin wrapper around the already-proven operatonService.deployDrd(), routing the CPSV Editor's own Deploy button through this backend instead of calling Operaton directly from the browser -- same CORS reasoning as the evaluate proxy above.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: dmn-validation.service.ts EXEC-* checks were all dead code
details: cprmvAttr()'s primary namespace-aware lookup called el.attr({ name, ns }) -- libxmljs2's setter overload, not a getter: it creates/sets an attribute and returns the element itself for chaining, which has no .value(). The throw was silently swallowed by the function's own catch, so EXEC-002 through EXEC-010 -- every rule-level and decision-level CPRMV validation check this service had ever shipped -- never actually fired, for any DMN, since the file was written. Fixed by dropping the broken setter-form branch and reading attributes via a direct attrs() scan.

Also fixed: CPRMV_NS was hardcoded to the legacy cprmv.open-regels.nl/0.3.0/ namespace, so a DMN using the current standaarden.open-regels.nl/standards/cprmv/0.4.1# namespace would short-circuit on an EXEC-001 "CPRMV not declared" before reaching any check -- CPRMV_NAMESPACES now accepts both.
New EXEC-011/EXEC-012 checks validate cell-level dct:source/cprmv:isBasedOn format on grounded DMN cells; EXEC-013 closes a pre-existing gap where cprmv:extends' format was never checked at all.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Bump seed versions so shellId reaches existing users' example sub-processes
details: example_tree_felling, example_zorgtoeslag_provisional, and example_zorgtoeslag_final's seed data got shellId added in an earlier commit, but their EXAMPLE_VERSIONS entries weren't bumped, so seed() skipped re-saving them for existing users -- both localStorage and Postgres kept the shellId-less copy, which falls back to the old ambiguous bpmnProcessId match and renders under every shell sharing that id.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: E2E badge color changed from indigo to orange
details: Indigo read too close to EXAMPLE's blue in practice. Orange is clearly distinct from every other badge color in use (blue/amber/green/violet/teal).

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Persist shellId and e2e status through Postgres, not just localStorage
details: Both bugs traced to the same cause: hydrateFromServer() treats the Postgres-backed server list as authoritative and replaces local state with it on every BpmnModeler mount. The two fields added for the e2e-fixtures work in the previous two commits never reached the database, so they didn't survive that replace.

process_definitions.status had CHECK (status IN ('example', 'wip')) -- no 'e2e'. Saving an e2e-status BPMN process violated the constraint and the save failed silently (fetch() doesn't reject on non-2xx responses). shellId was never part of the DB schema, upsert, or list query, so every hydrate overwrote the local, correctly-classified copy with the server's shellId-less one -- the shell/subprocess duplication fix from the previous two commits never actually held past the first render.
Adds shell_id to process_definitions (additive, idempotent) and widens the status CHECK to include 'e2e'. Threads shellId through the mapper, upsert, list query, and the frontend's save request.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Disambiguate shell/subprocess matching by shellId, not just bpmnProcessId
details: Shell/subprocess matching keyed purely on calledElement === shell.bpmnProcessId, a string that's no longer unique once a shell is deliberately duplicated -- an e2e-fixtures copy of a seeded example shell intentionally keeps the same bpmnProcessId, since that's the real production Operaton key. ProcessList's catalog grouping rendered every subprocess under *every* shell sharing its bpmnProcessId instead of just its own.

Adds shellId (holding the parent shell's own local record id) alongside the existing calledElement; grouping and BpmnModeler's language/organization propagation now prefer shellId when present, falling back to the old match for records saved before this field existed. Also wires E2E badge detection for imported BPMN processes off the existing e2e-fixtures textAnnotation marker.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: E2E status badge for imported e2e-fixtures forms and documents
details: Imported e2e-fixtures files rendered as generic WIP/DRAFT, indistinguishable from arbitrary in-progress work. Adds a new 'e2e' status, detected at import time from a self-describing marker baked into each fixture file: a wrapper key on forms (stripped before handing the schema to form-js) and the fixture's own status field on documents.
Extracts a shared StatusBadge component used by ProcessList, FormList and DocumentList, replacing three near-identical inline badge blocks and adding the new E2E badge to all three in one place.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Normalise line endings to LF via .gitattributes
details: The backend's .prettierrc sets endOfLine: lf, but the repo had no .gitattributes, so a Windows checkout with core.autocrlf=true produced CRLF working files and npm run format:check failed on already-correctly-formatted content -- a loop no commit could fix, since Git kept renormalising files straight back to CRLF. Forcing LF in the working tree closes the loop; batch files stay pinned to CRLF and images are marked binary.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Make CPRMV attribute rules actually fire (cprmvAttr namespaced lookup was broken)
details: cprmvAttr() tried el.attr({ name, ns: CPRMV_NS }) before falling back to a scan of el.attrs(). In libxmljs2 0.37 that object form is not a namespaced lookup: it sets attributes literally called "name" and "ns" on the element and returns a value with no .value() method, so the call threw. The function's own try/catch swallowed the throw and returned null, so the working attrs() fallback beneath it was never reached -- EXEC-002..EXEC-010 and CON-001..CON-003 never fired for any input, so ten validation rules were dead while reporting a clean result, and every inspected element was mutated with two junk attributes.

Dropping the object-form fast path is the whole fix. Verified against all 16 tracked .dmn files: no newly-reported issues, since none carried cprmv:* attributes at the time -- the rules now work for RONL DMN+ files that do.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Raise backend statement coverage from 17% to 98%
details: Adds 31 test files covering every previously-untested backend module and extends 3 existing ones. No production code changed. Statements 16.79% -> 98.06%, branches 18.10% -> 89.18%, tests 118 -> 1078 across 48 suites.

Previously at 0%: all 11 untested route modules, routes/index and routes/registry, 8 untested services, db/pool, db/migrate, utils/logger and utils/rootViews. Module-level singletons (db/pool, utils/logger, utils/config) are re-imported per test case via jest.isolateModules with a patched environment; @rdfjs/dataset and rdf-validate-shacl (ESM-only) are stubbed so the SHACL suite exercises layer loading and issue mapping rather than the RDF libraries themselves.

Documented (not fixed here, as a testing-scope decision) the cprmvAttr() defect fixed two commits later in this release: calling el.attr({ name, ns }) throws in libxmljs2 0.37 instead of performing a namespaced lookup, leaving ten validation rules permanently inert.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Fix an E2E fixture's BPMN schema error
details: Operaton's BPMN parser rejected TreeFellingPermitSubProcessE2E.bpmn (ENGINE-09005, a businessRuleTask found where an artifact-group element was expected) because the fixture-warning textAnnotation/association pair immediately preceded the file's first businessRuleTask. Every other fixture with the same annotation pattern has a scriptTask in that position instead, which validates fine, so this specific adjacency had never been submitted to Operaton for real parsing before. Fixed by moving the annotation to the end of the process body — after all flow elements, before the closing tag — which is also the more conventional placement for BPMN artifacts.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Give e2e-fixtures sub-processes their own Operaton keys
details: TreeFellingPermitSubProcess and ZorgtoeslagProvisionalSubProcess renamed to TreeFellingPermitSubProcessE2E / ZorgtoeslagProvisionalSubProcessE2E (filename, bpmn:process id, and the calling shell's callActivity calledElement). Prevents LDE's own process catalog from conflating the e2e-fixtures copy with the seeded-examples copy of the same sub-process — both previously shared the same bpmn:process id, so importing/redeploying the fixture could silently reuse the example's stale content instead. Shells (AwbShellProcess, AwbZorgtoeslagProcess) and RipR21Process are unaffected.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Resolve shared DMN decisions as untenanted from tenant-scoped business-rule-tasks
details: Confirmed empirically against a live Operaton instance: by default, a business-rule-task's camunda:decisionRef resolves against a decision definition under the exact same tenant-id as the calling process instance, with no fallback to a shared, untenanted decision even when one exists. camunda:decisionRefTenantId can override this, but only as an EL expression evaluating to null (${null}) — a literal empty string is silently ignored. Applied to all 7 business-rule-tasks across the 4 fixture BPMNs that reference genuinely tenant-agnostic, shared regulatory-logic DMN tables, so they keep resolving correctly now that the calling processes themselves carry a real tenant-id.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Fix a copy-paste processKey bug and nest sub-process fixtures under their shell
details: ZORGTOESLAG_PROVISIONAL_BESCHIKKING's processKey read 'AwbShellProcess' — copy-pasted from the tree-felling document template above it — corrected to 'AwbZorgtoeslagProcess', the process it actually belongs to; the regenerated .document fixture matches the corrected source exactly.

AwbShellProcess calls TreeFellingPermitSubProcess and AwbZorgtoeslagProcess calls ZorgtoeslagProvisionalSubProcess via a BPMN callActivity, which BpmnModeler.tsx auto-detects and bundles into a single deployment call — the manifest now nests each sub-process's fixture entry under its shell's own subProcesses array instead of listing it as a flat sibling, with a new test asserting each shell's BPMN genuinely contains a calledElement matching its declared nested sub-process keys.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Assemble the e2e-fixtures test bundle
details: A new, dedicated e2e-fixtures/<tenant>/ directory with a manifest.json and an integrity test, replacing two pre-existing, already-diverged 'examples' locations (broad stale reference material, and the general-purpose seeded-example store used by the BPMN Modeler's load-example buttons) as the single source of truth for ronl-business-api's E2E test suite. AwbShellProcess, TreeFellingPermitSubProcess, and AwbZorgtoeslagProcess/ZorgtoeslagProvisionalSubProcess are seeded from the proven-freshest examples copy; RipR21Process is assembled by merging two divergent draft folders (a swimlane redesign missing several of its own form files, filled in from an older, complete draft) and renamed from RipPhase1Process. Also adds the two decision-document fixtures (example_treefelling_beschikking, example_zorgtoeslag_provisional_beschikking) that both seeded BPMNs reference but had no corresponding .document file for anywhere in the repo, converted from their DocumentTemplate source objects.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Make organization mandatory when deploying a BPMN process
details: The BPMN Modeler's Deploy action now requires an Organization value before it will submit a deployment, sent to Operaton as its native tenant-id (POST /deployment/create's tenant-id field) — closing the gap where a process could be deployed with no tenant-id at all, invisible to any tenant-scoped lookup an application later needs to make against it.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Spec: mandatory organization/tenantId at BPMN deploy time
details: Design doc for making organization mandatory at deploy time and sending it to Operaton as native tenant-id, the foundation this release's e2e-fixtures work and ronl-business-api's own tenant-mandatory adoption both build on.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Add Ede and Gelderland to DSO Viewer location presets
details: Extends the DSO Viewer's activities-tab LOCATION_PRESETS with the municipality of Ede and the province of Gelderland, alongside the existing Lelystad and Flevoland entries. This one array drives both the location filter buttons and the authority-name lookup used when importing forms, so no other code changes were needed.

OINs were sourced from overheid.nl's Identificatiecodes records for each organization and cross-checked structurally: each OIN embeds the org's own RSIN, and both new values follow the same 00000001<RSIN>000 pattern as the existing Lelystad/Flevoland entries.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: DMN validator misses id-attribute deploy failures, false-positives on multi-word FEEL names
details: Adds BIZ-010 through BIZ-014, flagging <input>/<output>/<rule>/<inputEntry>/<outputEntry> elements missing the id attribute as errors. Operaton's DMN transformer requires id on these decision-table clause elements even though the DMN 1.3 XSD marks it optional, and rejects such files with DMN-02011 at deploy time — a class of failure this validator previously reported as fully valid.

Fixes two false-positive sources in INT-007. FEEL names may legally contain spaces, and a bare <inputExpression> that is itself one multi-word declared name (e.g. "natuurlijke persoon.woonachtig in de gemeente waar wordt aangevraagd") was being shredded word-by-word by the identifier tokenizer, with every word flagged as an unresolved variable; a whole-string match against declared/produced names is now tried first, before falling back to tokenization. Separately, FEEL_RESERVED was missing the single-word FEEL date/time component functions (year, month, day, hour, minute, second) alongside the already-excluded date/time/duration/number/string built-ins, so year(...) calls were flagging "year" itself as unresolved.

Found while debugging amsterdam/individuele-inkomenstoeslag-iknow.dmn's Operaton deploy failure in the CPSV Editor (ttl-editor) repo — together these fixes reduced that file's Interaction Rules warnings from 83 to 12. The residual 12 (multi-word names embedded inside compound expressions rather than as bare references, plus one likely real DRD-wiring gap in the source DMN) are documented as open issues rather than fixed, since closing them properly needs a materially larger longest-match tokenizer change.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: P7 — coverage report + CI-wiring deferral decision
details: Closes out the testing plan with a real --coverage run across both packages: 109 backend tests but only 13.82% backend statement coverage (the tested files are near-100%, but large route/service files — dmn.routes.ts, operaton.service.ts, sparql.service.ts, dmn-validation.service.ts, dso.service.ts and others — remain entirely untested), against 557 frontend tests at 74.03% statement coverage across 59 files, where P4–P6 reached every component/page/service directory at least once.

Decision: no CI test step is added to the Azure workflows yet, blocking or non-blocking — the same call ronl-business-api made at 83.39% coverage with its full P1–P11 backlog done, applied here specifically because the backend gap is breadth (whole files never touched) rather than depth (dense sub-branches in already-tested files). Documented in TESTING-GUIDE.md's new "CI roadmap (P7)" section, with the condition for revisiting it: once backend breadth improves, or the team decides breadth alone is an acceptable bar to gate on.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Frontend P6.8 — App.tsx + Changelog.tsx integration coverage (P6 complete)
details: Adds 31 tests across the final P6 phase — the top-level integration components that route between everything else. App.tsx (838 lines) renders 12 feature components plus executeSparqlQuery, all mocked as clickable/inspectable stubs, isolating the orchestrator's own state machine: sidebar navigation across all 12 views, localStorage viewMode persistence (with fallback on an invalid stored value), the always-mounted-but-CSS-hidden DmnValidator/ShaclValidator panes, the SPARQL run/error/auto-visualize-on-?s-?p-?o flow, the sample-query library, the settings panel (endpoint add/delete/reset, the DSO pre/prod toggle persisting to its own localStorage key), Orchestration-view cache refresh, and CSV export.

Changelog.tsx (5 tests) mocks changelog.json with a small two-entry fixture — one commits-format entry, one legacy sections-format entry — rather than asserting against the real, constantly-growing release data, covering both rendering paths plus expand/collapse.

One pre-existing, unrelated quirk surfaced and documented rather than fixed: the error overlay lives inside App's "Right Panel," which is itself hidden whenever viewMode is Orchestration — so a failed cache-refresh (triggered only from that view) sets the error state correctly but has no visible surface until the user navigates elsewhere.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Frontend P6.7 — DocumentComposer component coverage (tiptap + dnd-kit phase)
details: Adds 74 tests across DocumentComposer's 9 files — the heaviest remaining directory, coupling both @tiptap/react and @dnd-kit together. TextBlockEditor.tsx exercises real @tiptap/react/ProseMirror rather than mocking it outright (unlike bpmn-js/@bpmn-io/form-js in P6.5/P6.6), since ProseMirror is DOM/contenteditable-based and works under jsdom once two gaps are polyfilled locally: Range.prototype.getClientRects/getBoundingClientRect (called by EditorView.scrollToSelection on every transaction) and document.elementFromPoint (called by ProseMirror's mousedown handler via posAtCoords).

DocumentCanvas.tsx turned out to have no direct dnd-kit hook coupling of its own — it receives dragEndEvent/dragOverEvent as props computed by the parent's DndContext and resolves drops in a plain useEffect — so its full drag-end resolution matrix (new-block-add, cross-zone move, same-zone reorder, cross-zone reorder-to-position) was tested by constructing fake DragEndEvent objects and driving the effect via rerender(), no dnd-kit gesture simulation needed. DocumentComposer.tsx itself (the orchestrator) follows the same mocked-children-as-stubs pattern as ChainBuilder/FormEditor/BpmnModeler, covering bootstrap seeding, template CRUD, Save/Save As/Export/Close, and binding management.

One fixture-ordering bug caught while writing the orchestrator's tests: an early version of the "Save As does nothing when the prompt is cancelled" test seeded its mock store with only one template, not accounting for the component's own bootstrap effect seeding the two missing DEFAULT_TEMPLATES entries on mount — calling saveTemplate twice before the user ever clicked anything. Fixed by seeding the store with all defaults already present, matching the baseline the other CRUD tests use.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Adopt CalVer (YYYY.MM.patch) versioning for /bump-release
details: Patches .claude/commands/bump-release.md with the same CalVer scheme already adopted for the CPSV Editor: YYYY.MM.patch, patch resets to 0 on the first release of a new month, incremented for same-month follow-ups. Version-string convention only — no git tags, no generate-changelog.mjs, no versions.json — and applies only going forward; historical SemVer entries (1.9.13, 1.9.12, ...) are left as-is. The CalVer sequence is product-wide, not per-scope, so a backend-only and a frontend-only release still share the same next-in-sequence number.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Frontend P6.6 — BpmnModeler component coverage (bpmn-js canvas phase)
details: Adds 78 tests across BpmnModeler's 9 files. bpmn-js/lib/Modeler and bpmn-js-properties-panel are mocked outright — a small fake modeler class exposing just the canvas/eventBus/overlays/elementRegistry/propertiesPanel/modeling surface BpmnCanvas.tsx actually calls, built inside a vi.hoisted block so it exists before the hoisted vi.mock factory needs it. Covers XML import, Save/Export/Close, zoom controls, element-type-driven properties-panel injection (BusinessRuleTask → DMN selector, UserTask → Form+Document selectors, StartEvent → Form selector only), and the full deploy-to-Operaton modal (resource discovery, ronl:ropaRef-missing warning, board-owner auto-detection from candidateGroups, and both success/failure deploy responses).

The five small selector components (FormTemplateSelector, RopaSelector, DocumentTemplateSelector, DsoActiviteitSelector, DmnTemplateSelector) plus BpmnProperties/ProcessList have no third-party coupling and were tested first to establish the pattern. BpmnModeler.tsx itself (the orchestrator) mocks its already-tested ProcessList/BpmnCanvas children as clickable stubs, same pattern used for ChainBuilder/FormEditor — covering process CRUD, shell-to-subprocess language/organization propagation on save, footer-draft plumbing, and the seven versioned example-process seeding effect.

One pre-existing, unrelated quirk surfaced and documented rather than silently patched: the deploy modal's process-key extraction (doc.querySelector('process')) never matches a namespace-prefixed <bpmn:process> element under jsdom's XML parser — the component's own fallback to the literal string "process" always wins for XML shaped like real bpmn-js output.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Frontend P6.5 — FormEditor component coverage (first embedded-editor phase)
details: Adds 36 tests across FormEditor's 3 files — the first full embedded-editor-library phase. @bpmn-io/form-js is mocked outright (a small fake editor class covering importSchema/saveSchema/on/off/destroy) since exercising the real library in jsdom would mean mounting a full canvas editor. Covers FormList (no third-party coupling — grouping, search, .form file import via a real File/FileReader), FormCanvas (dirty-state tracking via the editor's changed event, Save/Export/destroy-on-unmount), and FormEditor's own orchestration (create/import/load/save/rename/delete, the stale-example seeding effect, and the unsaved-changes confirm gate).

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Frontend P6.4 — ChainBuilder component coverage (first dnd-kit phase)
details: Adds 102 tests across ChainBuilder's 13 files — the first @dnd-kit-coupled phase. useDraggable/useSortable/useDroppable all render fine without a DndContext/SortableContext wrapper in tests, since dnd-kit's context hooks fall back to sane defaults with no provider present — no special setup needed for the drag-and-drop coupling itself.

Covers the smaller presentational pieces (badges, execution progress, results, input form, vendor modal, export modal, semantic view, test-case panel) plus DmnList/ChainComposer (the actual dnd-kit-coupled panels), ChainConfig (template browser + save-as-DRD flow), and ChainBuilder.tsx itself (DMN/semantic-link loading, chain validation, preset loading incl. synthetic DRD models, and chain execution) — with its children mocked as clickable stubs to isolate the orchestrator's own state machine. Deliberately not covered: the actual @dnd-kit pointer-drag gesture, since handleDragEnd's own logic is exercised indirectly through the preset-loading and remove/clear tests.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Frontend P6.3 — DsoExplorer component coverage
details: Adds 21 tests for DsoExplorer.tsx — the largest single-file component tested so far (1,464 lines, one default export covering three tabs: Concepts, Works, Activities). dsoService is mocked via vi.mock + vi.importActual so the pure URL/URN helpers stay real while only the network-calling exports are replaced. Covers all three tabs' search/pagination, the Works tab's master-detail werkzaamheid panel, and the Activities tab's location presets, OIN-mode name filter, direct URN inspection, and applicable-rules section (STTR/DMN download links, the CPSV Editor DMN-publish handoff, and the DSO-to-LDE form-scaffold import flow).

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Frontend P6.2 — RopaEditor component coverage
details: Adds 60 tests across RopaEditor's 3 files. RopaList and the RopaEditor container are straightforward; RopaRecordEditor (the four-tab record editor) is the largest single component test file at this point — record fields, the legal-basis SPARQL lookup, the "hydrate from linked forms" flow, the BPMN-link tab's ronl:ropaRef read/write, and the status tab's confirm-gated "Set Active" transition.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Frontend P6.1 — Tutorial component coverage
details: Adds 9 tests for the Tutorial component — no third-party coupling, picked as the smallest P6 target to establish the RTL rendering pattern. tutorial.json is mocked with a small fixture rather than asserted against the real ~5-tutorial content.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Frontend P6.0 — components/common, plus the full P6 sub-phase breakdown
details: Adds 20 tests for components/common (ArtefactListToolbar, LanguageSelector, OrganizationSelector) — the smallest, least third-party-coupled directory, picked first to establish the RTL rendering pattern before the editor-wrapping directories.

Patches TESTING-GUIDE.md with a full P6.0–P6.8 sub-phase breakdown, worked out once P6 actually started: coupling-severity groups first (none → a drag-and-drop utility → one embedded editor library → two), size ascending within each group, top-level integration components last.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Frontend P5 — service layer coverage (msw + localStorage)
details: Adds 60 tests across the frontend's 11 service modules (ropaService, documentService, formService, bpmnService, assetService, templateService, sparqlService, dsoService, testCaseStorage, userTemplateStorage, defaultTestCases) — msw for the network-calling ones, plain jsdom localStorage for the two storage modules, raw fetch mocking for sparqlService's CORS-proxy fallback logic. Fixed a real cross-test-pollution bug in assetService.ts's module-level cache (tests now use distinct dataset names per test) and an msw path-param auto-decoding gotcha in the RopaService URL-encoding test.

commits.subject: Frontend P4 — Vitest bootstrap + pure-logic utils coverage
details: Adds Vitest, @testing-library/react/jest-dom/user-event, jsdom, and msw as frontend devDependencies. vite.config.ts's defineConfig now comes from vitest/config; test.environment defaults to 'node' with a per-file // @vitest-environment jsdom opt-in, matching ronl-business-api's frontend convention. Adds exportFormats.test.ts, exampleVersions.test.ts, testData.test.ts, and logoResolver.test.ts (39 tests total, all but one genuinely unreachable defensive branch at 100% coverage).

exportService.ts and bpmnTemplates.ts are deliberately deferred and documented in TESTS.md rather than silently skipped: exportService.ts only exports 2 of 6 functions, the rest reachable only through real DOM manipulation + JSZip archive building; bpmnTemplates.ts is confirmed pure static XML template data.

commits.author: Steven Gort

details: Adds route integration tests for ropa.public.routes.ts, assets.public.routes.ts, process.routes.ts, dmn-xml.routes.ts, and health.routes.ts (15 tests total) — each mounted in isolation (a fresh express() app per file, not the full index.ts), with the service layer mocked and supertest driving the requests.

commits.subject: Backend P1 — errors, error.middleware, version.middleware
details: Adds errors.test.ts (23 tests, 100%), error.middleware.test.ts (5 tests, logger.ts mocked to avoid its real winston/filesystem side effects), and version.middleware.test.ts (3 tests). Adds docs/TESTS.md documenting P0+P1: per-file test inventories and both tooling gaps found while getting the first test file working.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Backend P0 — jest.config.js, first real test, fix two latent tooling gaps
details: Adds packages/backend/jest.config.js (ts-jest preset, collectCoverageFrom across all of src/**/*.ts so untested files report as 0% instead of being omitted) and src/utils/etag.test.ts (11 tests). npm test now exits 0 with real assertions instead of "No tests found, exiting with code 1".

Root package.json gets a "test": "npm run test --workspaces --if-present" script, matching ronl-business-api's convention exactly.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Add TESTING-GUIDE.md — phased testing strategy for backend + frontend
details: Covers Analysis, Plan, and Phased approach, mirroring the CPSV Editor's guide but adapted for this repo's actual shape: a real Express backend (Jest already installed, zero tests, npm test currently exits 1 with "no tests found") alongside a Vite/React frontend with no test tooling at all but no bundler migration to sequence around either.
